                  u32::from_str_radix(hex, 16).map_err(|_| self.err(\"bad \\\\u escape\"))?;\n                            self.pos += 4;\n                            if (0xD800..=0xDBFF).contains(&code) {\n                                // High surrogate; require low surrogate.\n                                if self.b.get(self.pos..self.pos + 2) != Some(b\"\\\\u\") {\n                                    return Err(self.err(\"expected low surrogate\"));\n                                }\n                                self.pos += 2;\n                                if self.pos + 4 > self.b.len() {\n                                    return Err(self.err(\"bad surrogate pair\"));\n                                }\n                                let hex2 = std::str::from_utf8(&self.b[self.pos..self.pos + 4])\n                                    .map_err(|_| self.err(\"bad surrogate pair\"))?;\n                                let low = u32::from_str_radix(hex2, 16)\n                                    .map_err(|_| self.err(\"bad surrogate pair\"))?;\n                                self.pos += 4;\n                                if !(0xDC00..=0xDFFF).contains(&low) {\n                                    return Err(self.err(\"bad low surrogate\"));\n                                }\n                                let c = s.push(char::from_u32(c).ok_or(self.err(\"bad surrogate codepoint\"))?);\n                            } else {\n                                s.push(char::from_u32(code).ok_or(self.err(\"bad codepoint\"))?);\n                            }\n                        }\n                        _ => return Err(self.err(\"bad escape\")),\n                    }\n                }\n         self.pos += 5;\n            Ok(Json::Bool(false))\n        } else {\n            Err(self.err(\"invalid literal\"))\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn null(&mut self) -> Result<Json, ParseError> {\n fn number(&mut self) -> Result<Json, ParseError> {\n        let start = self.pos;\n        if self.peek() == Some(b'-') {\n            self.pos += 1;\n        }\n        let digit_start = self.pos;\n text.parse::<i64>()\n            .map(Json::Int)\n            .map_err(|_| self.err(\"integer out of range\"))\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    #[test]\n    fn again);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn rejects_bad_json() {\n        assert!(parse(\"\").is_err());\n        assert!(parse(\"{\").is_err());\n        assert!(parse(\"[1,]\").is_err());\n        assert!(parse(r#\"{\"a\":}\"#).is_err());\n        assert!(parse(\"1.5\").is_err());\n        assert!(parse(\"01\").is_err());\n        assert!(parse(r#\"\"bad \"#).is_err());\n        assert!(parse(\"null x\").is_err());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn unicode_escape() {\n        let v = parse(r#\"\"é é 😀\"\"#).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(v.as_str(), Some(\"é é 😀\"));\n {"parentUuid":"92f178f9-251c-41de-a552-e4786953c6a7","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_1e8x33h5arafa19xkrtjmaib","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp10/a/src/merkle.rs","content":"//! Merkle tree over fixed-size blocks of a file.\n//!\n//! # Canonical hashing rules\n//!\n//! - Leaf `i` committing to block bytes `b`:\n//!   `SHA256( 0x00 || i_be_u64 || b.len()_be_u64 || b )`\n//!   Index and length are inside the hash, so blocks cannot be reordered and\n//!   the final (short) block cannot be padded to forge a different file length.\n//! - Internal node with children L, R:\n//!   `SHA256( 0x01 || L || R )`\n//! - **Odd-node rule** (Certificate-Transparency style): when a level has an\n//!   odd number of nodes, the last node is promoted to the next level\n//!   unchanged — it is NOT duplicated and NOT hashed with itself.\n//! - Empty file (zero leaves): root is the fixed sentinel\n//!   `SHA256(\"merkle-store:empty-root-v1\")`, distinct by construction from any\n//!   leaf/internal hash.\n//!\n//! # Range proofs\n//!\n//! A proof for blocks `[start, end)` contains:\n//! 1. the leaf hashes for every requested block (recomputed by the verifier\n//!    from the supplied block bytes), and\n//! 2. sibling/sub-tree hashes needed to rebuild the root, each tagged with its\n//!    `(level, index)` so reordered or misplaced nodes (\"错位证明\") are rejected\n//!    structurally, before any hash comparison.\n//!\n//! The verifier only touches the bytes of the requested blocks plus the O(log n)\n//! proof hashes; it never reads the complete file.\n\nuse crate::sha256::sha256;\n\npub type Hash32 = [u8; 32];\n\nconst LEAF_DOMAIN: u8 = 0x00;\nconst INTERNAL_DOMAIN: u8 = 0x01;\nconst EMPTY_ROOT_TAG: &[u8] = b\"merkle-store:empty-root-v1\";\n\n/// Root of the zero-leaf tree.\npub fn empty_root() -> Hash32 {\n    sha256(EMPTY_ROOT_TAG)\n}\n\n/// Commitment of block `index` to its exact bytes.\npub fn leaf_hash(index: usize, block: &[u8]) -> Hash32 {\n    let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 8 + 8 + block.len());\n    input.push(LEAF_DOMAIN);\n    input.extend_from_slice(&(index as u64).to_be_bytes());\n    input.extend_from_slice(&(block.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());\n    input.extend_from_slice(block);\n    sha256(&input)\n}\n\n/// Commitment of an ordered pair of child nodes.\npub fn internal_hash(left: &Hash32, right: &Hash32) -> Hash32 {\n    let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 64);\n    input.push(INTERNAL_DOMAIN);\n    input.extend_from_slice(left);\n    input.extend_from_slice(right);\n    sha256(&input)\n}\n\n/// Number of nodes `level` holds for a tree with `n` leaves.\npub fn level_count(n: usize, level: usize) -> usize {\n    let mut c = n;\n    for _ in 0..level {\n        c = (c + 1) / 2;\n    }\n    c\n}\n\n/// Build all levels from leaf hashes. `result[0]` is the leaves themselves.\npub fn build_levels(leaves: &[Hash32]) -> Vec<Vec<Hash32>> {\n    let mut levels: Vec<Vec<Hash32>> = Vec::new();\n    levels.push(leaves.to_vec());\n    while levels.last().unwrap().len() > 1 {\n        let cur = levels.last().unwrap();\n        let mut next = Vec::with_capacity((cur.len() + 1) / 2);\n        let mut i = 0;\n        while i + 1 < cur.len() {\n            next.push(internal_hash(&cur[i], &cur[i + 1]));\n            i += 2;\n        }\n        if i < cur.len() {\n            // Odd trailing node: promote unchanged.\n            next.push(cur[i]);\n        }\n        levels.push(next);\n    }\n    levels\n}\n\n/// Full-tree root from leaf hashes (the reference implementation the\n/// incremental updater must agree with).\npub fn rebuild_root(leaves: &[Hash32]) -> Hash32 {\n    if leaves.is_empty() {\n        return empty_root();\n    }\n    let levels = build_levels(leaves);\n    levels.last().unwrap()[0]\n}\n\n/// One hash in a range proof, positioned canonically in the tree.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ProofNode {\n    pub level: usize,\n    pub index: usize,\n    pub hash: Hash32,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct RangeProof {\n    /// Total number of leaves in the tree.\n    pub n: usize,\n    /// Requested half-open range of leaf indices.\n    pub start: usize,\n    pub end: usize,\n    /// Ordered: range leaves first (level 0, ascending index), then siblings\n    /// level by level from the bottom, left sibling before right sibling.\n    pub nodes: Vec<ProofNode>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ProofError {\n    /// start >= end on a non-empty tree.\n    EmptyRange,\n    /// Range or node falls outside the declared tree.\n    OutOfRange,\n    /// n==0 but range was not exactly [0,0).\n    BadEmptyRange,\n    /// Proof ended before the root was reconstructed.\n    ProofTooShort,\n    /// Proof carried nodes that reconstruction did not consume.\n    ProofTooLong,\n    /// A proof node appeared at a different (level,index) than required.\n    MisalignedNode {\n        expected_level: usize,\n        expected_index: usize,\n        got_level: usize,\n        got_index: usize,\n    },\n    /// Recomputed leaf hash does not match the proof (block bytes tampered).\n    LeafMismatch { index: usize },\n    /// Declared data length disagrees with the declared leaf count.\n    LengthMismatch,\n    /// Reconstructed root differs from the trusted root.\n    RootMismatch,\n    /// Empty file proven against a non-empty (or wrong) root.\n    EmptyRootMismatch,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ProofError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ProofError::EmptyRange => write!(f, \"empty proof range [start,end)\"),\n            ProofError::OutOfRange => write!(f, \"proof range exceeds declared leaf count\"),\n            ProofError::BadEmptyRange => write!(f, \"zero-leaf tree requires range [0,0)\"),\n            ProofError::ProofTooShort => write!(f, \"proof truncated before reaching the root\"),\n            ProofError::ProofTooLong => write!(f, \"proof contains unconsumed nodes\"),\n            ProofError::MisalignedNode { expected_level, expected_index, got_level, got_index } => {\n                write!(\n                    f,\n                    \"misaligned proof node: expected node ({expected_level},{expected_index}), got ({got_level},{got_index})\"\n                )\n            }\n            ProofError::LeafMismatch { index } => {\n                write!(f, \"leaf {index} hash mismatch with supplied block bytes\")\n            }\n            ProofError::LengthMismatch => {\n                write!(f, \"declared byte length disagrees with leaf count and block size\")\n            }\n            ProofError::RootMismatch => write!(f, \"reconstructed root does not match trusted root\"),\n            ProofError::EmptyRootMismatch => {\n                write!(f, \"zero-leaf tree root does not match empty-root sentinel\")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for ProofError {}\n\nfn validate_range(n: usize, start: usize, end: usize) -> Result<(), ProofError> {\n    if n == 0 {\n        if start != 0 || end != 0 {\n            return Err(ProofError::BadEmptyRange);\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n    if start >= end {\n        return Err(ProofError::EmptyRange);\n    }\n    if start > end || end > n {\n        return Err(ProofError::OutOfRange);\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Generate a range proof, sourcing leaf and internal hashes via closures.\n///\n/// `node(level, index)` returns the canonical node stored at that position;\n/// level 0 reads leaves.\npub fn prove<F>(n: usize, start: usize, end: usize, node: F) -> Result<RangeProof, ProofError>\nwhere\n    F: Fn(usize, usize) -> Hash32,\n{\n    validate_range(n, start, end)?;\n    let mut nodes = Vec::new();\n    if n == 0 {\n        return Ok(RangeProof { n, start, end, nodes });\n    }\n\n    let mut lo = start;\n    let mut hi = end;\n    let mut count = n;\n    let mut level = 0usize;\n    loop {\n        // Known nodes at this level: exactly the range [lo, hi). At level 0\n        // these are leaves, which we always include so the verifier can bind\n        // them to the supplied block bytes.\n        if level == 0 {\n            for i in lo..hi {\n                nodes.push(ProofNode { level, index: i, hash: node(level, i) });\n            }\n        }\n        if count == 1 {\n            break;\n        }\n        // Left sibling: lo is odd, so it is the right half of a pair.\n        if lo % 2 == 1 {\n            nodes.push(ProofNode { level, index: lo - 1, hash: node(level, lo - 1) });\n        }\n        // Right sibling: (hi-1) is even and has a partner still in the level.\n        if hi % 2 == 1 && hi < count {\n            nodes.push(ProofNode { level, index: hi, hash: node(level, hi) });\n        }\n        lo /= 2;\n        hi = hi.div_ceil(2);\n        count = (count + 1) / 2;\n        level += 1;\n    }\n    Ok(RangeProof { n, start, end, nodes })\n}\n\n/// Verify a range proof against a trusted root and the actual block bytes.\n///\n/// `blocks` holds the bytes of exactly blocks `[start, end)`, in order. The\n/// verifier recomputes leaf hashes itself; any length or content forgery in\n/// the blocks is detected here.\npub fn verify(\n    proof: &RangeProof,\n    block_size: u64,\n    data_len: u64,\n    expected_root: &Hash32,\n    blocks: &[Vec<u8>],\n) -> Result<(), ProofError> {\n    let RangeProof { n, start, end, nodes } = proof;\n    let (n, start, end) = (*n, *start, *end);\n\n    // Length binding: the declared byte count must encode exactly n blocks.\n    let expect_n = if data_len == 0 { 0 } else { ((data_len - 1) / block_size + 1) as usize };\n    if expect_n != n {\n        return Err(ProofError::LengthMismatch);\n    }\n    validate_range(n, start, end)?;\n    if blocks.len() != end - start {\n        return Err(ProofError::LengthMismatch);\n    }\n\n    // Empty file: the only valid proof is the empty one against the sentinel.\n    if n == 0 {\n        if !nodes.is_empty() {\n            return Err(ProofError::ProofTooLong);\n        }\n        if expected_root != &empty_root() {\n            return Err(ProofError::EmptyRootMismatch);\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let mut cursor = 0usize;\n    let take = |cursor: &mut usize| -> Result<&ProofNode, ProofError> {\n        let node = nodes.get(*cursor).ok_or(ProofError::ProofTooShort)?;\n        *cursor += 1;\n        Ok(node)\n    };\n    let expect_tag = |node: &ProofNode, level: usize, index: usize| -> Result<(), ProofError> {\n        if node.level != level || node.index != index {\n            return Err(ProofError::MisalignedNode {\n                expected_level: level,\n                expected_index: index,\n                got_level: node.level,\n                got_index: node.index,\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    };\n\n    // 1. Leaves: recompute from block bytes and bind to the provided nodes.\n    let mut cur: Vec<Hash32> = Vec::with_capacity(end - start);\n    for (k, bytes) in blocks.iter().enumerate() {\n        let i = start + k;\n        let want_len = if i + 1 == n {\n            (data_len - (i as u64) * block_size) as usize\n        } else {\n            block_size as usize\n        };\n        if bytes.len() != want_len {\n            return Err(ProofError::LengthMismatch);\n        }\n        let node = take(&mut cursor)?;\n        expect_tag(node, 0, i)?;\n        let recomputed = leaf_hash(i, bytes);\n        if recomputed != node.hash {\n            return Err(ProofError::LeafMismatch { index: i });\n        }\n        cur.push(recomputed);\n    }\n\n    // 2. Climb level by level, consuming exactly the required siblings.\n    let mut lo = start;\n    let mut hi = end;\n    let mut count = n;\n    let mut level = 0usize;\n    while count > 1 {\n        if lo % 2 == 1 {\n            let node = take(&mut cursor)?;\n            expect_tag(node, level, lo - 1)?;\n            cur.insert(0, node.hash);\n            lo -= 1;\n        }\n        if hi % 2 == 1 && hi < count {\n            let node = take(&mut cursor)?;\n            expect_tag(node, level, hi)?;\n            cur.push(node.hash);\n            hi += 1;\n        }\n        // Pair everything up at this level (range is now even-aligned and\n        // covers an even number of slots; an odd trailing node of the whole\n        // tree only ever appears inside cur via promotion below).\n        let mut next = Vec::with_capacity(cur.len().div_ceil(2));\n        let mut i = 0;\n        while i + 1 < cur.len() {\n            next.push(internal_hash(&cur[i], &cur[i + 1]));\n            i += 2;\n        }\n        if i < cur.len() {\n            // Odd trailing node promoted unchanged — only possible when this\n            // level itself had odd count.\n            next.push(cur[i]);\n        }\n        cur = next;\n        lo /= 2;\n        hi = hi.div_ceil(2);\n        count = (count + 1) / 2;\n        level += 1;\n    }\n\n    // 3. Exactly one root node must remain.\n    if cur.len() != 1 {\n        return Err(ProofError::ProofTooShort);\n    }\n    if cursor != nodes.len() {\n        return Err(ProofError::ProofTooLong);\n    }\n    if cur[0] != *expected_root {\n        return Err(ProofError::RootMismatch);\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// JSON (de)serialization of proofs.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nuse crate::base64;\nuse crate::json::{self, Json};\n\npub fn proof_to_json(p: &RangeProof) -> Json {\n    Json::Array(\n        p.nodes\n            .iter()\n            .map(|nd| {\n                json::obj(vec![\n                    (\"level\", Json::Int(nd.level as i64)),\n                    (\"index\", Json::Int(nd.index as i64)),\n                    (\"hash\", Json::Str(base64::encode(&nd.hash))),\n                ])\n            })\n            .collect(),\n    )\n}\n\npub fn proof_from_json(\n    n: usize,\n    start: usize,\n    end: usize,\n    value: &Json,\n) -> Result<RangeProof, String> {\n    let arr = value.as_array().ok_or(\"proof nodes must be an array\")?;\n    let mut nodes = Vec::with_capacity(arr.len());\n    for item in arr {\n        let level = item.get(\"level\").and_then(Json::as_i64).ok_or(\"node.level missing\")?;\n        let index = item.get(\"index\").and_then(Json::as_i64).ok_or(\"node.index missing\")?;\n        let hash_s = item.get(\"hash\").and_then(Json::as_str).ok_or(\"node.hash missing\")?;\n        let bytes = base64::decode(hash_s).map_err(|_| \"node.hash not valid base64\")?;\n        if bytes.len() != 32 || level < 0 || index < 0 {\n            return Err(\"node.hash must decode to 32 bytes\".into());\n        }\n        let mut hash = [0u8; 32];\n        hash.copy_from_slice(&bytes);\n        nodes.push(ProofNode { level: level as usize, index: index as usize, hash });\n    }\n    Ok(RangeProof { n, start, end, nodes })\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn blocks(data: &[u8], size: u64) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {\n        data.chunks(size as usize).map(|c| c.to_vec()).collect()\n    }\n\n    fn leaves_of(bs: &[Vec<u8>]) -> Vec<Hash32> {\n        bs.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, b)| leaf_hash(i, b)).collect()\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn leaf_and_internal_domains_differ() {\n        // A leaf hash can never be confused with an internal hash.\n        let h = leaf_hash(0, &[1, 32]);\n        let internal = internal_hash(&h, &h);\n        assert_ne!(h, internal);\n        assert_ne!(h, empty_root());\n        assert_ne!(internal, empty_root());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_file_root_is_sentinel() {\n        assert_eq!(rebuild_root(&[]), empty_root());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn odd_rule_does_not_duplicate() {\n        // For 3 leaves the promoted leaf must appear in level 1 verbatim.\n        let l = vec![leaf_hash(0, b\"a\"), leaf_hash(1, b\"b\"), leaf_hash(2, b\"c\")];\n        let levels = build_levels(&l);\n        assert_eq!(levels.len(), 3);\n        assert_eq!(levels[1].len(), 2);\n        assert_eq!(levels[1][1], l[2]); // promoted, not hash(c,c)\n        assert_eq!(levels[1][0], internal_hash(&l[0], &l[1]));\n        assert_eq!(levels[2].len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(levels[2][0], internal_hash(&levels[1][0], &levels[1][1]));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn all_ranges_verify_for_many_sizes() {\n        for size in 1u64..=6 {\n            for nblocks in 0usize..12 {\n                let data: Vec<u8> = (0..(nblocks as u64 * size))\n                    .map(|i| (i % 251) as u8)\n                    .collect();\n                let bs = blocks(&data, size);\n                assert_eq!(bs.len(), nblocks);\n                let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n                let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n                let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n\n                if nblocks == 0 {\n                    let p = prove(0, 0, 0, node).unwrap();\n                    assert!(p.nodes.is_empty());\n                    verify(&p, size, 0, &root, &[]).unwrap();\n                    continue;\n                }\n                for start in 0..nblocks {\n                    for end in start + 1..=nblocks {\n                        let p = prove(nblocks, start, end, node).unwrap();\n                        let slice = bs[start..end].to_vec();\n                        verify(&p, size, data.len() as u64, &root, &slice).unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n                            panic!(\"n={nblocks} range {start}..{end} size {size}: {e}\")\n                        });\n                        // Proof size never exceeds range + 2*height.\n                        let mut h = 1;\n                        let mut c = nblocks;\n                        while c > 1 { c = (c + 1) / 2; h += 1; }\n                        assert!(p.nodes.len() <= (end - start) + 2 * (h - 1));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn full_range_needs_no_siblings() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcdefgh\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        let p = prove(4, 0, 4, node).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(p.nodes.len(), 4);\n        assert!(p.nodes.iter().all(|nd| nd.level == 0));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn first_and_last_single_block_ranges() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcde\", 2); // 3 blocks: ab cd e\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        // First block.\n        let p0 = prove(3, 0, 1, node).unwrap();\n        verify(&p0, 2, 5, &root, &[b\"ab\".to_vec()]).unwrap();\n        // Last (short) block.\n        let p2 = prove(3, 2, 3, node).unwrap();\n        verify(&p2, 2, 5, &root, &[b\"e\".to_vec()]).unwrap();\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tampered_block_detected() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcde\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        let p = prove(3, 0, 1, node).unwrap();\n        let err = verify(&p, 2, 5, &root, &[b\"XB\".to_vec()]).unwrap_err();\n        assert_eq!(err, ProofError::LeafMismatch { index: 0 });\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn forged_lengths_detected() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcde\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        let p = prove(3, 2, 3, node).unwrap();\n\n        // Claim a longer file: last block padded to full size.\n        assert_eq!(\n            verify(&p, 2, 6, &root, &[b\"e\\0\".to_vec()]).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::LengthMismatch\n        );\n        // Claim a shorter file: computed n disagrees with proof.n.\n        assert_eq!(\n            verify(&p, 2, 4, &root, &[b\"e\".to_vec()]).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::LengthMismatch\n        );\n        // Right length, wrong trusted root.\n        let wrong = [0u8; Merkle tree over fixed-size blocks of a file.\n//!\n//! # Canonical hashing rules\n//!\n//! - Leaf `i` committing to block bytes `b`:\n//!   `SHA256( 0x00 || i_be_u64 || b.len()_be_u64 || b )`\n//!   Index and length are inside the hash, so blocks cannot be reordered and\n//!   the final (short) block cannot be padded to forge a different file length.\n//! - Internal node with children L, R:\n//!   `SHA256( 0x01 || L || R )`\n//! - **Odd-node rule** (Certificate-Transparency style): when a level has an\n//!   odd number of nodes, the last node is promoted to the next level\n//!   unchanged — it is NOT duplicated and NOT hashed with itself.\n//! - Empty file (zero leaves): root is the fixed sentinel\n//!   `SHA256(\"merkle-store:empty-root-v1\")`, distinct by construction from any\n//!   leaf/internal hash.\n//!\n//! # Range proofs\n//!\n//! A proof for blocks `[start, end)` contains:\n//! 1. the leaf hashes for every requested block (recomputed by the verifier\n//!    from the supplied block bytes), and\n//! 2. sibling/sub-tree hashes needed to rebuild the root, each tagged with its\n//!    `(level, index)` so reordered or misplaced nodes (\"错位证明\") are rejected\n//!    structurally, before any hash comparison.\n//!\n//! The verifier only touches the bytes of the requested blocks plus the O(log n)\n//! proof hashes; it never reads the complete file.\n\nuse crate::sha256::sha256;\n\npub type Hash32 = [u8; 32];\n\nconst LEAF_DOMAIN: u8 = 0x00;\nconst INTERNAL_DOMAIN: u8 = 0x01;\nconst EMPTY_ROOT_TAG: &[u8] = b\"merkle-store:empty-root-v1\";\n\n/// Root of the zero-leaf tree.\npub fn empty_root() -> Hash32 {\n    sha256(EMPTY_ROOT_TAG)\n}\n\n/// Commitment of block `index` to its exact bytes.\npub fn leaf_hash(index: usize, block: &[u8]) -> Hash32 {\n    let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 8 + 8 + block.len());\n    input.push(LEAF_DOMAIN);\n    input.extend_from_slice(&(index as u64).to_be_bytes());\n    input.extend_from_slice(&(block.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());\n    input.extend_from_slice(block);\n    sha256(&input)\n}\n\n/// Commitment of an ordered pair of child nodes.\npub fn internal_hash(left: &Hash32, right: &Hash32) -> Hash32 {\n    let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 64);\n    input.push(INTERNAL_DOMAIN);\n    input.extend_from_slice(left);\n    input.extend_from_slice(right);\n    sha256(&input)\n}\n\n/// Number of nodes `level` holds for a tree with `n` leaves.\npub fn level_count(n: usize, level: usize) -> usize {\n    let mut c = n;\n    for _ in 0..level {\n        c = (c + 1) / 2;\n    }\n    c\n}\n\n/// Build all levels from leaf hashes. `result[0]` is the leaves themselves.\npub fn build_levels(leaves: &[Hash32]) -> Vec<Vec<Hash32>> {\n    let mut levels: Vec<Vec<Hash32>> = Vec::new();\n    levels.push(leaves.to_vec());\n    while levels.last().unwrap().len() > 1 {\n        let cur = levels.last().unwrap();\n        let mut next = Vec::with_capacity((cur.len() + 1) / 2);\n        let mut i = 0;\n        while i + 1 < cur.len() {\n            next.push(internal_hash(&cur[i], &cur[i + 1]));\n            i += 2;\n        }\n        if i < cur.len() {\n            // Odd trailing node: promote unchanged.\n            next.push(cur[i]);\n        }\n        levels.push(next);\n    }\n    levels\n}\n\n/// Full-tree root from leaf hashes (the reference implementation the\n/// incremental updater must agree with).\npub fn rebuild_root(leaves: &[Hash32]) -> Hash32 {\n    if leaves.is_empty() {\n        return empty_root();\n    }\n    let levels = build_levels(leaves);\n    levels.last().unwrap()[0]\n}\n\n/// One hash in a range proof, positioned canonically in the tree.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ProofNode {\n    pub level: usize,\n    pub index: usize,\n    pub hash: Hash32,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct RangeProof {\n    /// Total number of leaves in the tree.\n    pub n: usize,\n    /// Requested half-open range of leaf indices.\n    pub start: usize,\n    pub end: usize,\n    /// Ordered: range leaves first (level 0, ascending index), then siblings\n    /// level by level from the bottom, left sibling before right sibling.\n    pub nodes: Vec<ProofNode>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ProofError {\n    /// start >= end on a non-empty tree.\n    EmptyRange,\n    /// Range or node falls outside the declared tree.\n    OutOfRange,\n    /// n==0 but range was not exactly [0,0).\n    BadEmptyRange,\n    /// Proof ended before the root was reconstructed.\n    ProofTooShort,\n    /// Proof carried nodes that reconstruction did not consume.\n    ProofTooLong,\n    /// A proof node appeared at a different (level,index) than required.\n    MisalignedNode {\n        expected_level: usize,\n        expected_index: usize,\n        got_level: usize,\n        got_index: usize,\n    },\n    /// Recomputed leaf hash does not match the proof (block bytes tampered).\n    LeafMismatch { index: usize },\n    /// Declared data length disagrees with the declared leaf count.\n    LengthMismatch,\n    /// Reconstructed root differs from the trusted root.\n    RootMismatch,\n    /// Empty file proven against a non-empty (or wrong) root.\n    EmptyRootMismatch,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ProofError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ProofError::EmptyRange => write!(f, \"empty proof range [start,end)\"),\n            ProofError::OutOfRange => write!(f, \"proof range exceeds declared leaf count\"),\n            ProofError::BadEmptyRange => write!(f, \"zero-leaf tree requires range [0,0)\"),\n            ProofError::ProofTooShort => write!(f, \"proof truncated before reaching the root\"),\n            ProofError::ProofTooLong => write!(f, \"proof contains unconsumed nodes\"),\n            ProofError::MisalignedNode { expected_level, expected_index, got_level, got_index } => {\n                write!(\n                    f,\n                    \"misaligned proof node: expected node ({expected_level},{expected_index}), got ({got_level},{got_index})\"\n                )\n            }\n            ProofError::LeafMismatch { index } => {\n                write!(f, \"leaf {index} hash mismatch with supplied block bytes\")\n            }\n            ProofError::LengthMismatch => {\n                write!(f, \"declared byte length disagrees with leaf count and block size\")\n            }\n            ProofError::RootMismatch => write!(f, \"reconstructed root does not match trusted root\"),\n            ProofError::EmptyRootMismatch => {\n                write!(f, \"zero-leaf tree root does not match empty-root sentinel\")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for ProofError {}\n\nfn validate_range(n: usize, start: usize, end: usize) -> Result<(), ProofError> {\n    if n == 0 {\n        if start != 0 || end != 0 {\n            return Err(ProofError::BadEmptyRange);\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n    if start >= end {\n        return Err(ProofError::EmptyRange);\n    }\n    if start > end || end > n {\n        return Err(ProofError::OutOfRange);\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Generate a range proof, sourcing leaf and internal hashes via closures.\n///\n/// `node(level, index)` returns the canonical node stored at that position;\n/// level 0 reads leaves.\npub fn prove<F>(n: usize, start: usize, end: usize, node: F) -> Result<RangeProof, ProofError>\nwhere\n    F: Fn(usize, usize) -> Hash32,\n{\n    validate_range(n, start, end)?;\n    let mut nodes = Vec::new();\n    if n == 0 {\n        return Ok(RangeProof { n, start, end, nodes });\n    }\n\n    let mut lo = start;\n    let mut hi = end;\n    let mut count = n;\n    let mut level = 0usize;\n    loop {\n        // Known nodes at this level: exactly the range [lo, hi). At level 0\n        // these are leaves, which we always include so the verifier can bind\n        // them to the supplied block bytes.\n        if level == 0 {\n            for i in lo..hi {\n                nodes.push(ProofNode { level, index: i, hash: node(level, i) });\n            }\n        }\n        if count == 1 {\n            break;\n        }\n        // Left sibling: lo is odd, so it is the right half of a pair.\n        if lo % 2 == 1 {\n            nodes.push(ProofNode { level, index: lo - 1, hash: node(level, lo - 1) });\n        }\n        // Right sibling: (hi-1) is even and has a partner still in the level.\n        if hi % 2 == 1 && hi < count {\n            nodes.push(ProofNode { level, index: hi, hash: node(level, hi) });\n        }\n        lo /= 2;\n        hi = hi.div_ceil(2);\n        count = (count + 1) / 2;\n        level += 1;\n    }\n    Ok(RangeProof { n, start, end, nodes })\n}\n\n/// Verify a range proof against a trusted root and the actual block bytes.\n///\n/// `blocks` holds the bytes of exactly blocks `[start, end)`, in order. The\n/// verifier recomputes leaf hashes itself; any length or content forgery in\n/// the blocks is detected here.\npub fn verify(\n    proof: &RangeProof,\n    block_size: u64,\n    data_len: u64,\n    expected_root: &Hash32,\n    blocks: &[Vec<u8>],\n) -> Result<(), ProofError> {\n    let RangeProof { n, start, end, nodes } = proof;\n    let (n, start, end) = (*n, *start, *end);\n\n    // Length binding: the declared byte count must encode exactly n blocks.\n    let expect_n = if data_len == 0 { 0 } else { ((data_len - 1) / block_size + 1) as usize };\n    if expect_n != n {\n        return Err(ProofError::LengthMismatch);\n    }\n    validate_range(n, start, end)?;\n    if blocks.len() != end - start {\n        return Err(ProofError::LengthMismatch);\n    }\n\n    // Empty file: the only valid proof is the empty one against the sentinel.\n    if n == 0 {\n        if !nodes.is_empty() {\n            return Err(ProofError::ProofTooLong);\n        }\n        if expected_root != &empty_root() {\n            return Err(ProofError::EmptyRootMismatch);\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let mut cursor = 0usize;\n    let take = |cursor: &mut usize| -> Result<&ProofNode, ProofError> {\n        let node = nodes.get(*cursor).ok_or(ProofError::ProofTooShort)?;\n        *cursor += 1;\n        Ok(node)\n    };\n    let expect_tag = |node: &ProofNode, level: usize, index: usize| -> Result<(), ProofError> {\n        if node.level != level || node.index != index {\n            return Err(ProofError::MisalignedNode {\n                expected_level: level,\n                expected_index: index,\n                got_level: node.level,\n                got_index: node.index,\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    };\n\n    // 1. Leaves: recompute from block bytes and bind to the provided nodes.\n    let mut cur: Vec<Hash32> = Vec::with_capacity(end - start);\n    for (k, bytes) in blocks.iter().enumerate() {\n        let i = start + k;\n        let want_len = if i + 1 == n {\n            (data_len - (i as u64) * block_size) as usize\n        } else {\n            block_size as usize\n        };\n        if bytes.len() != want_len {\n            return Err(ProofError::LengthMismatch);\n        }\n        let node = take(&mut cursor)?;\n        expect_tag(node, 0, i)?;\n        let recomputed = leaf_hash(i, bytes);\n        if recomputed != node.hash {\n            return Err(ProofError::LeafMismatch { index: i });\n        }\n        cur.push(recomputed);\n    }\n\n    // 2. Climb level by level, consuming exactly the required siblings.\n    let mut lo = start;\n    let mut hi = end;\n    let mut count = n;\n    let mut level = 0usize;\n    while count > 1 {\n        if lo % 2 == 1 {\n            let node = take(&mut cursor)?;\n            expect_tag(node, level, lo - 1)?;\n            cur.insert(0, node.hash);\n            lo -= 1;\n        }\n        if hi % 2 == 1 && hi < count {\n            let node = take(&mut cursor)?;\n            expect_tag(node, level, hi)?;\n            cur.push(node.hash);\n            hi += 1;\n        }\n        // Pair everything up at this level (range is now even-aligned and\n        // covers an even number of slots; an odd trailing node of the whole\n        // tree only ever appears inside cur via promotion below).\n        let mut next = Vec::with_capacity(cur.len().div_ceil(2));\n        let mut i = 0;\n        while i + 1 < cur.len() {\n            next.push(internal_hash(&cur[i], &cur[i + 1]));\n            i += 2;\n        }\n        if i < cur.len() {\n            // Odd trailing node promoted unchanged — only possible when this\n            // level itself had odd count.\n            next.push(cur[i]);\n        }\n        cur = next;\n        lo /= 2;\n        hi = hi.div_ceil(2);\n        count = (count + 1) / 2;\n        level += 1;\n    }\n\n    // 3. Exactly one root node must remain.\n    if cur.len() != 1 {\n        return Err(ProofError::ProofTooShort);\n    }\n    if cursor != nodes.len() {\n        return Err(ProofError::ProofTooLong);\n    }\n    if cur[0] != *expected_root {\n        return Err(ProofError::RootMismatch);\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// JSON (de)serialization of proofs.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nuse crate::base64;\nuse crate::json::{self, Json};\n\npub fn proof_to_json(p: &RangeProof) -> Json {\n    Json::Array(\n        p.nodes\n            .iter()\n            .map(|nd| {\n                json::obj(vec![\n                    (\"level\", Json::Int(nd.level as i64)),\n                    (\"index\", Json::Int(nd.index as i64)),\n                    (\"hash\", Json::Str(base64::encode(&nd.hash))),\n                ])\n            })\n            .collect(),\n    )\n}\n\npub fn proof_from_json(\n    n: usize,\n    start: usize,\n    end: usize,\n    value: &Json,\n) -> Result<RangeProof, String> {\n    let arr = value.as_array().ok_or(\"proof nodes must be an array\")?;\n    let mut nodes = Vec::with_capacity(arr.len());\n    for item in arr {\n        let level = item.get(\"level\").and_then(Json::as_i64).ok_or(\"node.level missing\")?;\n        let index = item.get(\"index\").and_then(Json::as_i64).ok_or(\"node.index missing\")?;\n        let hash_s = item.get(\"hash\").and_then(Json::as_str).ok_or(\"node.hash missing\")?;\n        let bytes = base64::decode(hash_s).map_err(|_| \"node.hash not valid base64\")?;\n        if bytes.len() != 32 || level < 0 || index < 0 {\n            return Err(\"node.hash must decode to 32 bytes\".into());\n        }\n        let mut hash = [0u8; 32];\n        hash.copy_from_slice(&bytes);\n        nodes.push(ProofNode { level: level as usize, index: index as usize, hash });\n    }\n    Ok(RangeProof { n, start, end, nodes })\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn blocks(data: &[u8], size: u64) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {\n        data.chunks(size as usize).map(|c| c.to_vec()).collect()\n    }\n\n    fn leaves_of(bs: &[Vec<u8>]) -> Vec<Hash32> {\n        bs.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, b)| leaf_hash(i, b)).collect()\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn leaf_and_internal_domains_differ() {\n        // A leaf hash can never be confused with an internal hash.\n        let h = leaf_hash(0, &[1, 32]);\n        let internal = internal_hash(&h, &h);\n        assert_ne!(h, internal);\n        assert_ne!(h, empty_root());\n        assert_ne!(internal, empty_root());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_file_root_is_sentinel() {\n        assert_eq!(rebuild_root(&[]), empty_root());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn odd_rule_does_not_duplicate() {\n        // For 3 leaves the promoted leaf must appear in level 1 verbatim.\n        let l = vec![leaf_hash(0, b\"a\"), leaf_hash(1, b\"b\"), leaf_hash(2, b\"c\")];\n        let levels = build_levels(&l);\n        assert_eq!(levels.len(), 3);\n        assert_eq!(levels[1].len(), 2);\n        assert_eq!(levels[1][1], l[2]); // promoted, not hash(c,c)\n        assert_eq!(levels[1][0], internal_hash(&l[0], &l[1]));\n        assert_eq!(levels[2].len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(levels[2][0], internal_hash(&levels[1][0], &levels[1][1]));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn all_ranges_verify_for_many_sizes() {\n        for size in 1u64..=6 {\n            for nblocks in 0usize..12 {\n                let data: Vec<u8> = (0..(nblocks as u64 * size))\n                    .map(|i| (i % 251) as u8)\n                    .collect();\n                let bs = blocks(&data, size);\n                assert_eq!(bs.len(), nblocks);\n                let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n                let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n                let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n\n                if nblocks == 0 {\n                    let p = prove(0, 0, 0, node).unwrap();\n                    assert!(p.nodes.is_empty());\n                    verify(&p, size, 0, &root, &[]).unwrap();\n                    continue;\n                }\n                for start in 0..nblocks {\n                    for end in start + 1..=nblocks {\n                        let p = prove(nblocks, start, end, node).unwrap();\n                        let slice = bs[start..end].to_vec();\n                        verify(&p, size, data.len() as u64, &root, &slice).unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n                            panic!(\"n={nblocks} range {start}..{end} size {size}: {e}\")\n                        });\n                        // Proof size never exceeds range + 2*height.\n                        let mut h = 1;\n                        let mut c = nblocks;\n                        while c > 1 { c = (c + 1) / 2; h += 1; }\n                        assert!(p.nodes.len() <= (end - start) + 2 * (h - 1));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn full_range_needs_no_siblings() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcdefgh\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        let p = prove(4, 0, 4, node).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(p.nodes.len(), 4);\n        assert!(p.nodes.iter().all(|nd| nd.level == 0));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn first_and_last_single_block_ranges() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcde\", 2); // 3 blocks: ab cd e\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        // First block.\n        let p0 = prove(3, 0, 1, node).unwrap();\n        verify(&p0, 2, 5, &root, &[b\"ab\".to_vec()]).unwrap();\n        // Last (short) block.\n        let p2 = prove(3, 2, 3, node).unwrap();\n        verify(&p2, 2, 5, &root, &[b\"e\".to_vec()]).unwrap();\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tampered_block_detected() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcde\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        let p = prove(3, 0, 1, node).unwrap();\n        let err = verify(&p, 2, 5, &root, &[b\"XB\".to_vec()]).unwrap_err();\n        assert_eq!(err, ProofError::LeafMismatch { index: 0 });\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn forged_lengths_detected() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcde\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        let p = prove(3, 2, 3, node).unwrap();\n\n        // Claim a longer file: last block padded to full size.\n        assert_eq!(\n            verify(&p, 2, 6, &root, &[b\"e\\0\".to_vec()]).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::LengthMismatch\n        );\n        // Claim a shorter file: computed n disagrees with proof.n.\n        assert_eq!(\n            verify(&p, 2, 4, &root, &[b\"e\".to_vec()]).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::LengthMismatch\n        );\n        // Right length, wrong trusted root.\n        let wrong = [0u8; 32];\n        assert_eq!(\n            verify(&p, 2, 5, &wrong, &[b\"e\".to_vec()]).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::RootMismatch\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn misaligned_and_resized_proofs_detected() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcdefgh\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        let good = prove(4, 1, 2, node).unwrap();\n        let data = vec![b\"cd\".to_vec()];\n\n        // Swap two proof nodes.\n        let mut swapped = good.clone();\n        swapped.nodes.swap(1, 2);\n        assert!(matches!(\n            verify(&swapped, 2, 8, &root, &data).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::MisalignedNode { .. }\n        ));\n\n        // Drop a node.\n        let mut truncated = good.clone();\n        truncated.nodes.pop();\n        assert_eq!(\n            verify(&truncated, 2, 8, &root, &data).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::ProofTooShort\n        );\n\n        // Append a bogus node.\n        let mut extended = good.clone();\n        extended.nodes.push(ProofNode { level: 9, index: 9, hash: [7u8; 32] });\n        assert_eq!(\n            verify(&extended, 2, 8, &root, &data).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::ProofTooLong\n        );\n\n        // Forge a tag without touching hashes.\n        let mut retagged = good.clone();\n        retagged.nodes[1].index = 2;\n        assert!(matches!(\n            verify(&retagged, 2, 8, &root, &data).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::MisalignedNode { .. }\n        ));\n\n        // Range outside the tree.\n        let bad = prove(4, 0, 5, node).unwrap_err();\n        assert_eq!(bad, ProofError::OutOfRange);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_range_rejected_on_nonempty_tree() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"ab\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        assert_eq!(prove(1, 0, 0, node).unwrap_err(), ProofError::EmptyRange);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn proof_json_roundtrip() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcde\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        let p = prove(3, 0, 2, node).unwrap();\n        let j = proof_to_json(&p);\n        let p2 = proof_from_json(3, 0, 2, &j).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(p, p2);\n    }\n}\n","file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp10/a/src/merkle.rs"}},"apiBlockIndex":2,"type":"assistant","uuid":"59079175-b6f5-40f4-83fe-ec48e98e30e9","timestamp":"2026-09-23T01:39:05.321Z","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"7f404cf2-9b88-493e-b8e2-bb5bcd9a4e01","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp10/a","sessionId":"7f404cf2-9b88-493e-b8e2-bb5bcd9a4e01","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp10-a","slug":"steady-napping-thunder"}

Merkle tree over fixed-size blocks of a file.\n//!\n//! # Canonical hashing rules\n//!\n//! - Leaf `i` committing to block bytes `b`:\n//!   `SHA256( 0x00 || i_be_u64 || b.len()_be_u64 || b )`\n//!   Index and length are inside the hash, so blocks cannot be reordered and\n//!   the final (short) block cannot be padded to forge a different file length.\n//! - Internal node with children L, R:\n//!   `SHA256( 0x01 || L || R )`\n//! - **Odd-node rule** (Certificate-Transparency style): when a level has an\n//!   odd number of nodes, the last node is promoted to the next level\n//!   unchanged — it is NOT duplicated and NOT hashed with itself.\n//! - Empty file (zero leaves): root is the fixed sentinel\n//!   `SHA256(\"merkle-store:empty-root-v1\")`, distinct by construction from any\n//!   leaf/internal hash.\n//!\n//! # Range proofs\n//!\n//! A proof for blocks `[start, end)` contains:\n//! 1. the leaf hashes for every requested block (recomputed by the verifier\n//!    from the supplied block bytes), and\n//! 2. sibling/sub-tree hashes needed to rebuild the root, each tagged with its\n//!    `(level, index)` so reordered or misplaced nodes (\"错位证明\") are rejected\n//!    structurally, before any hash comparison.\n//!\n//! The verifier only touches the bytes of the requested blocks plus the O(log n)\n//! proof hashes; it never reads the complete file.\n\nuse crate::sha256::sha256;\n\npub type Hash32 = [u8; 32];\n\nconst LEAF_DOMAIN: u8 = 0x00;\nconst INTERNAL_DOMAIN: u8 = 0x01;\nconst EMPTY_ROOT_TAG: &[u8] = b\"merkle-store:empty-root-v1\";\n\n/// Root of the zero-leaf tree.\npub fn empty_root() -> Hash32 {\n    sha256(EMPTY_ROOT_TAG)\n}\n\n/// Commitment of block `index` to its exact bytes.\npub fn leaf_hash(index: usize, block: &[u8]) -> Hash32 {\n    let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 8 + 8 + block.len());\n    input.push(LEAF_DOMAIN);\n    input.extend_from_slice(&(index as u64).to_be_bytes());\n    input.extend_from_slice(&(block.len() as u64).to_be_bytes());\n    input.extend_from_slice(block);\n    sha256(&input)\n}\n\n/// Commitment of an ordered pair of child nodes.\npub fn internal_hash(left: &Hash32, right: &Hash32) -> Hash32 {\n    let mut input = Vec::with_capacity(1 + 64);\n    input.push(INTERNAL_DOMAIN);\n    input.extend_from_slice(left);\n    input.extend_from_slice(right);\n    sha256(&input)\n}\n\n/// Number of nodes `level` holds for a tree with `n` leaves.\npub fn level_count(n: usize, level: usize) -> usize {\n    let mut c = n;\n    for _ in 0..level {\n        c = (c + 1) / 2;\n    }\n    c\n}\n\n/// Build all levels from leaf hashes. `result[0]` is the leaves themselves.\npub fn build_levels(leaves: &[Hash32]) -> Vec<Vec<Hash32>> {\n    let mut levels: Vec<Vec<Hash32>> = Vec::new();\n    levels.push(leaves.to_vec());\n    while levels.last().unwrap().len() > 1 {\n        let cur = levels.last().unwrap();\n        let mut next = Vec::with_capacity((cur.len() + 1) / 2);\n        let mut i = 0;\n        while i + 1 < cur.len() {\n            next.push(internal_hash(&cur[i], &cur[i + 1]));\n            i += 2;\n        }\n        if i < cur.len() {\n            // Odd trailing node: promote unchanged.\n            next.push(cur[i]);\n        }\n        levels.push(next);\n    }\n    levels\n}\n\n/// Full-tree root from leaf hashes (the reference implementation the\n/// incremental updater must agree with).\npub fn rebuild_root(leaves: &[Hash32]) -> Hash32 {\n    if leaves.is_empty() {\n        return empty_root();\n    }\n    let levels = build_levels(leaves);\n    levels.last().unwrap()[0]\n}\n\n/// One hash in a range proof, positioned canonically in the tree.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ProofNode {\n    pub level: usize,\n    pub index: usize,\n    pub hash: Hash32,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct RangeProof {\n    /// Total number of leaves in the tree.\n    pub n: usize,\n    /// Requested half-open range of leaf indices.\n    pub start: usize,\n    pub end: usize,\n    /// Ordered: range leaves first (level 0, ascending index), then siblings\n    /// level by level from the bottom, left sibling before right sibling.\n    pub nodes: Vec<ProofNode>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ProofError {\n    /// start >= end on a non-empty tree.\n    EmptyRange,\n    /// Range or node falls outside the declared tree.\n    OutOfRange,\n    /// n==0 but range was not exactly [0,0).\n    BadEmptyRange,\n    /// Proof ended before the root was reconstructed.\n    ProofTooShort,\n    /// Proof carried nodes that reconstruction did not consume.\n    ProofTooLong,\n    /// A proof node appeared at a different (level,index) than required.\n    MisalignedNode {\n        expected_level: usize,\n        expected_index: usize,\n        got_level: usize,\n        got_index: usize,\n    },\n    /// Recomputed leaf hash does not match the proof (block bytes tampered).\n    LeafMismatch { index: usize },\n    /// Declared data length disagrees with the declared leaf count.\n    LengthMismatch,\n    /// Reconstructed root differs from the trusted root.\n    RootMismatch,\n    /// Empty file proven against a non-empty (or wrong) root.\n    EmptyRootMismatch,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ProofError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            ProofError::EmptyRange => write!(f, \"empty proof range [start,end)\"),\n            ProofError::OutOfRange => write!(f, \"proof range exceeds declared leaf count\"),\n            ProofError::BadEmptyRange => write!(f, \"zero-leaf tree requires range [0,0)\"),\n            ProofError::ProofTooShort => write!(f, \"proof truncated before reaching the root\"),\n            ProofError::ProofTooLong => write!(f, \"proof contains unconsumed nodes\"),\n            ProofError::MisalignedNode { expected_level, expected_index, got_level, got_index } => {\n                write!(\n                    f,\n                    \"misaligned proof node: expected node ({expected_level},{expected_index}), got ({got_level},{got_index})\"\n                )\n            }\n            ProofError::LeafMismatch { index } => {\n                write!(f, \"leaf {index} hash mismatch with supplied block bytes\")\n            }\n            ProofError::LengthMismatch => {\n                write!(f, \"declared byte length disagrees with leaf count and block size\")\n            }\n            ProofError::RootMismatch => write!(f, \"reconstructed root does not match trusted root\"),\n            ProofError::EmptyRootMismatch => {\n                write!(f, \"zero-leaf tree root does not match empty-root sentinel\")\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for ProofError {}\n\nfn validate_range(n: usize, start: usize, end: usize) -> Result<(), ProofError> {\n    if n == 0 {\n        if start != 0 || end != 0 {\n            return Err(ProofError::BadEmptyRange);\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n    if start >= end {\n        return Err(ProofError::EmptyRange);\n    }\n    if start > end || end > n {\n        return Err(ProofError::OutOfRange);\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n/// Generate a range proof, sourcing leaf and internal hashes via closures.\n///\n/// `node(level, index)` returns the canonical node stored at that position;\n/// level 0 reads leaves.\npub fn prove<F>(n: usize, start: usize, end: usize, node: F) -> Result<RangeProof, ProofError>\nwhere\n    F: Fn(usize, usize) -> Hash32,\n{\n    validate_range(n, start, end)?;\n    let mut nodes = Vec::new();\n    if n == 0 {\n        return Ok(RangeProof { n, start, end, nodes });\n    }\n\n    let mut lo = start;\n    let mut hi = end;\n    let mut count = n;\n    let mut level = 0usize;\n    loop {\n        // Known nodes at this level: exactly the range [lo, hi). At level 0\n        // these are leaves, which we always include so the verifier can bind\n        // them to the supplied block bytes.\n        if level == 0 {\n            for i in lo..hi {\n                nodes.push(ProofNode { level, index: i, hash: node(level, i) });\n            }\n        }\n        if count == 1 {\n            break;\n        }\n        // Left sibling: lo is odd, so it is the right half of a pair.\n        if lo % 2 == 1 {\n            nodes.push(ProofNode { level, index: lo - 1, hash: node(level, lo - 1) });\n        }\n        // Right sibling: (hi-1) is even and has a partner still in the level.\n        if hi % 2 == 1 && hi < count {\n            nodes.push(ProofNode { level, index: hi, hash: node(level, hi) });\n        }\n        lo /= 2;\n        hi = hi.div_ceil(2);\n        count = (count + 1) / 2;\n        level += 1;\n    }\n    Ok(RangeProof { n, start, end, nodes })\n}\n\n/// Verify a range proof against a trusted root and the actual block bytes.\n///\n/// `blocks` holds the bytes of exactly blocks `[start, end)`, in order. The\n/// verifier recomputes leaf hashes itself; any length or content forgery in\n/// the blocks is detected here.\npub fn verify(\n    proof: &RangeProof,\n    block_size: u64,\n    data_len: u64,\n    expected_root: &Hash32,\n    blocks: &[Vec<u8>],\n) -> Result<(), ProofError> {\n    let RangeProof { n, start, end, nodes } = proof;\n    let (n, start, end) = (*n, *start, *end);\n\n    // Length binding: the declared byte count must encode exactly n blocks.\n    let expect_n = if data_len == 0 { 0 } else { ((data_len - 1) / block_size + 1) as usize };\n    if expect_n != n {\n        return Err(ProofError::LengthMismatch);\n    }\n    validate_range(n, start, end)?;\n    if blocks.len() != end - start {\n        return Err(ProofError::LengthMismatch);\n    }\n\n    // Empty file: the only valid proof is the empty one against the sentinel.\n    if n == 0 {\n        if !nodes.is_empty() {\n            return Err(ProofError::ProofTooLong);\n        }\n        if expected_root != &empty_root() {\n            return Err(ProofError::EmptyRootMismatch);\n        }\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n\n    let mut cursor = 0usize;\n    let take = |cursor: &mut usize| -> Result<&ProofNode, ProofError> {\n        let node = nodes.get(*cursor).ok_or(ProofError::ProofTooShort)?;\n        *cursor += 1;\n        Ok(node)\n    };\n    let expect_tag = |node: &ProofNode, level: usize, index: usize| -> Result<(), ProofError> {\n        if node.level != level || node.index != index {\n            return Err(ProofError::MisalignedNode {\n                expected_level: level,\n                expected_index: index,\n                got_level: node.level,\n                got_index: node.index,\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    };\n\n    // 1. Leaves: recompute from block bytes and bind to the provided nodes.\n    let mut cur: Vec<Hash32> = Vec::with_capacity(end - start);\n    for (k, bytes) in blocks.iter().enumerate() {\n        let i = start + k;\n        let want_len = if i + 1 == n {\n            (data_len - (i as u64) * block_size) as usize\n        } else {\n            block_size as usize\n        };\n        if bytes.len() != want_len {\n            return Err(ProofError::LengthMismatch);\n        }\n        let node = take(&mut cursor)?;\n        expect_tag(node, 0, i)?;\n        let recomputed = leaf_hash(i, bytes);\n        if recomputed != node.hash {\n            return Err(ProofError::LeafMismatch { index: i });\n        }\n        cur.push(recomputed);\n    }\n\n    // 2. Climb level by level, consuming exactly the required siblings.\n    let mut lo = start;\n    let mut hi = end;\n    let mut count = n;\n    let mut level = 0usize;\n    while count > 1 {\n        if lo % 2 == 1 {\n            let node = take(&mut cursor)?;\n            expect_tag(node, level, lo - 1)?;\n            cur.insert(0, node.hash);\n            lo -= 1;\n        }\n        if hi % 2 == 1 && hi < count {\n            let node = take(&mut cursor)?;\n            expect_tag(node, level, hi)?;\n            cur.push(node.hash);\n            hi += 1;\n        }\n        // Pair everything up at this level (range is now even-aligned and\n        // covers an even number of slots; an odd trailing node of the whole\n        // tree only ever appears inside cur via promotion below).\n        let mut next = Vec::with_capacity(cur.len().div_ceil(2));\n        let mut i = 0;\n        while i + 1 < cur.len() {\n            next.push(internal_hash(&cur[i], &cur[i + 1]));\n            i += 2;\n        }\n        if i < cur.len() {\n            // Odd trailing node promoted unchanged — only possible when this\n            // level itself had odd count.\n            next.push(cur[i]);\n        }\n        cur = next;\n        lo /= 2;\n        hi = hi.div_ceil(2);\n        count = (count + 1) / 2;\n        level += 1;\n    }\n\n    // 3. Exactly one root node must remain.\n    if cur.len() != 1 {\n        return Err(ProofError::ProofTooShort);\n    }\n    if cursor != nodes.len() {\n        return Err(ProofError::ProofTooLong);\n    }\n    if cur[0] != *expected_root {\n        return Err(ProofError::RootMismatch);\n    }\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// JSON (de)serialization of proofs.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nuse crate::base64;\nuse crate::json::{self, Json};\n\npub fn proof_to_json(p: &RangeProof) -> Json {\n    Json::Array(\n        p.nodes\n            .iter()\n            .map(|nd| {\n                json::obj(vec![\n                    (\"level\", Json::Int(nd.level as i64)),\n                    (\"index\", Json::Int(nd.index as i64)),\n                    (\"hash\", Json::Str(base64::encode(&nd.hash))),\n                ])\n            })\n            .collect(),\n    )\n}\n\npub fn proof_from_json(\n    n: usize,\n    start: usize,\n    end: usize,\n    value: &Json,\n) -> Result<RangeProof, String> {\n    let arr = value.as_array().ok_or(\"proof nodes must be an array\")?;\n    let mut nodes = Vec::with_capacity(arr.len());\n    for item in arr {\n        let level = item.get(\"level\").and_then(Json::as_i64).ok_or(\"node.level missing\")?;\n        let index = item.get(\"index\").and_then(Json::as_i64).ok_or(\"node.index missing\")?;\n        let hash_s = item.get(\"hash\").and_then(Json::as_str).ok_or(\"node.hash missing\")?;\n        let bytes = base64::decode(hash_s).map_err(|_| \"node.hash not valid base64\")?;\n        if bytes.len() != 32 || level < 0 || index < 0 {\n            return Err(\"node.hash must decode to 32 bytes\".into());\n        }\n        let mut hash = [0u8; 32];\n        hash.copy_from_slice(&bytes);\n        nodes.push(ProofNode { level: level as usize, index: index as usize, hash });\n    }\n    Ok(RangeProof { n, start, end, nodes })\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn blocks(data: &[u8], size: u64) -> Vec<Vec<u8>> {\n        data.chunks(size as usize).map(|c| c.to_vec()).collect()\n    }\n\n    fn leaves_of(bs: &[Vec<u8>]) -> Vec<Hash32> {\n        bs.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, b)| leaf_hash(i, b)).collect()\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn leaf_and_internal_domains_differ() {\n        // A leaf hash can never be confused with an internal hash.\n        let h = leaf_hash(0, &[1, 32]);\n        let internal = internal_hash(&h, &h);\n        assert_ne!(h, internal);\n        assert_ne!(h, empty_root());\n        assert_ne!(internal, empty_root());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_file_root_is_sentinel() {\n        assert_eq!(rebuild_root(&[]), empty_root());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn odd_rule_does_not_duplicate() {\n        // For 3 leaves the promoted leaf must appear in level 1 verbatim.\n        let l = vec![leaf_hash(0, b\"a\"), leaf_hash(1, b\"b\"), leaf_hash(2, b\"c\")];\n        let levels = build_levels(&l);\n        assert_eq!(levels.len(), 3);\n        assert_eq!(levels[1].len(), 2);\n        assert_eq!(levels[1][1], l[2]); // promoted, not hash(c,c)\n        assert_eq!(levels[1][0], internal_hash(&l[0], &l[1]));\n        assert_eq!(levels[2].len(), 1);\n        assert_eq!(levels[2][0], internal_hash(&levels[1][0], &levels[1][1]));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn all_ranges_verify_for_many_sizes() {\n        for size in 1u64..=6 {\n            for nblocks in 0usize..12 {\n                let data: Vec<u8> = (0..(nblocks as u64 * size))\n                    .map(|i| (i % 251) as u8)\n                    .collect();\n                let bs = blocks(&data, size);\n                assert_eq!(bs.len(), nblocks);\n                let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n                let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n                let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n\n                if nblocks == 0 {\n                    let p = prove(0, 0, 0, node).unwrap();\n                    assert!(p.nodes.is_empty());\n                    verify(&p, size, 0, &root, &[]).unwrap();\n                    continue;\n                }\n                for start in 0..nblocks {\n                    for end in start + 1..=nblocks {\n                        let p = prove(nblocks, start, end, node).unwrap();\n                        let slice = bs[start..end].to_vec();\n                        verify(&p, size, data.len() as u64, &root, &slice).unwrap_or_else(|e| {\n                            panic!(\"n={nblocks} range {start}..{end} size {size}: {e}\")\n                        });\n                        // Proof size never exceeds range + 2*height.\n                        let mut h = 1;\n                        let mut c = nblocks;\n                        while c > 1 { c = (c + 1) / 2; h += 1; }\n                        assert!(p.nodes.len() <= (end - start) + 2 * (h - 1));\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn full_range_needs_no_siblings() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcdefgh\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        let p = prove(4, 0, 4, node).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(p.nodes.len(), 4);\n        assert!(p.nodes.iter().all(|nd| nd.level == 0));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn first_and_last_single_block_ranges() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcde\", 2); // 3 blocks: ab cd e\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        // First block.\n        let p0 = prove(3, 0, 1, node).unwrap();\n        verify(&p0, 2, 5, &root, &[b\"ab\".to_vec()]).unwrap();\n        // Last (short) block.\n        let p2 = prove(3, 2, 3, node).unwrap();\n        verify(&p2, 2, 5, &root, &[b\"e\".to_vec()]).unwrap();\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn tampered_block_detected() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcde\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        let p = prove(3, 0, 1, node).unwrap();\n        let err = verify(&p, 2, 5, &root, &[b\"XB\".to_vec()]).unwrap_err();\n        assert_eq!(err, ProofError::LeafMismatch { index: 0 });\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn forged_lengths_detected() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcde\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        let p = prove(3, 2, 3, node).unwrap();\n\n        // Claim a longer file: last block padded to full size.\n        assert_eq!(\n            verify(&p, 2, 6, &root, &[b\"e\\0\".to_vec()]).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::LengthMismatch\n        );\n        // Claim a shorter file: computed n disagrees with proof.n.\n        assert_eq!(\n            verify(&p, 2, 4, &root, &[b\"e\".to_vec()]).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::LengthMismatch\n        );\n        // Right length, wrong trusted root.\n        let wrong = [0u8; 32];\n        assert_eq!(\n            verify(&p, 2, 5, &wrong, &[b\"e\".to_vec()]).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::RootMismatch\n        );\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn misaligned_and_resized_proofs_detected() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcdefgh\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let root = rebuild_root(&leaves);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        let good = prove(4, 1, 2, node).unwrap();\n        let data = vec![b\"cd\".to_vec()];\n\n        // Swap two proof nodes.\n        let mut swapped = good.clone();\n        swapped.nodes.swap(1, 2);\n        assert!(matches!(\n            verify(&swapped, 2, 8, &root, &data).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::MisalignedNode { .. }\n        ));\n\n        // Drop a node.\n        let mut truncated = good.clone();\n        truncated.nodes.pop();\n        assert_eq!(\n            verify(&truncated, 2, 8, &root, &data).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::ProofTooShort\n        );\n\n        // Append a bogus node.\n        let mut extended = good.clone();\n        extended.nodes.push(ProofNode { level: 9, index: 9, hash: [7u8; 32] });\n        assert_eq!(\n            verify(&extended, 2, 8, &root, &data).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::ProofTooLong\n        );\n\n        // Forge a tag without touching hashes.\n        let mut retagged = good.clone();\n        retagged.nodes[1].index = 2;\n        assert!(matches!(\n            verify(&retagged, 2, 8, &root, &data).unwrap_err(),\n            ProofError::MisalignedNode { .. }\n        ));\n\n        // Range outside the tree.\n        let bad = prove(4, 0, 5, node).unwrap_err();\n        assert_eq!(bad, ProofError::OutOfRange);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn empty_range_rejected_on_nonempty_tree() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"ab\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        assert_eq!(prove(1, 0, 0, node).unwrap_err(), ProofError::EmptyRange);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn proof_json_roundtrip() {\n        let bs = blocks(b\"abcde\", 2);\n        let leaves = leaves_of(&bs);\n        let node = |lvl: usize, idx: usize| build_levels(&leaves)[lvl][idx];\n        let p = prove(3, 0, 2, node).unwrap();\n        let j = proof_to_json(&p);\n        let p2 = proof_from_json(3, 0, 2, &j).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(p, p2);\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"59079175-b6f5-40f4-83fe-ec48e98e30e9","session_id":"7f404cf2-9b88-493e-b8e2-bb5bcd9a4e01","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp10/a","sessionId":"7f404cf2-9b88-493e-b8e2-bb5bcd9a4e01","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp10-a","slug":"steady-napping-thunder"}

Injectable I/O layer.\n//!\n//! All repository disk access goes through the [`Vfs`] trait:\n//! - [`RealVfs`] performs ordinary filesystem operations (with fsync and\n//!   atomic temp-file renames for the durability/sync boundaries);\n//! - [`MemVfs`] is an in-memory filesystem used by tests;\n//! - [`FaultyVfs`] wraps either implementation and injects I/O errors or byte\n//!   corruption on a selected call number, so crash/torn-write recovery can be\n//!   exercised without real disks.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\nuse std::io::{self, Read as _, Seek as _, SeekFrom, Write as _};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\npub trait Vfs: Send + Sync {\n    fn exists(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<bool>;\n    fn read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>>;\n    /// Overwrite atomically: write `tmp`, fsync, rename over target, fsync dir.\n    fn write_atomic(&self, path: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()>;\n    fn remove(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;\n    fn len(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<u64>;\n    fn read_at(&self, path: &Path, offset: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize>;\n    /// Create if missing (zero-filled) and overwrite bytes at `offset`.\n    fn write_at(&self, path: &Path, offset: u64, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()>;\n    fn truncate(&self, path: &Path, len: u64) -> io::Result<()>;\n    fn sync(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()>;\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Real filesystem.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\npub struct RealVfs;\n\nimpl RealVfs {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        RealVfs\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Default for RealVfs {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self::new()\n    }\n}\n\nfn sync_dir(path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n    let dir = path.parent().unwrap_or_else(|| Path::new(\".\"));\n    let f = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().read(true).open(dir)?;\n    f.sync_all()\n}\n\nimpl Vfs for RealVfs {\n    fn exists(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<bool> {\n        Ok(path.exists())\n    }\n\n    fn read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {\n        std::fs::read(path)\n    }\n\n    fn write_atomic(&self, path: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let mut tmp = PathBuf::from(path);\n        let file_name = tmp\n            .file_name()\n            .ok_or_else(|| io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, \"bad path\"))?\n            .to_owned();\n        tmp.set_file_name(format!(\".{}.tmp-{}\", file_name.to_string_lossy(), std::process::id()));\n        {\n            let mut f = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n                .write(true)\n                .create(true)\n                .truncate(true)\n                .open(&tmp)?;\n            f.write_all(data)?;\n            f.sync_all()?;\n        }\n        std::fs::rename(&tmp, path)?;\n        sync_dir(path)\n    }\n\n    fn remove(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        std::fs::remove_file(path)\n    }\n\n    fn len(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<u64> {\n        Ok(std::fs::metadata(path)?.len())\n    }\n\n    fn read_at(&self, path: &Path, offset: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {\n        let mut f = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().read(true).open(path)?;\n        f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(offset))?;\n        f.read(buf)\n    }\n\n    fn write_at(&self, path: &Path, offset: u64, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let mut f = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .write(true)\n            .create(true)\n            .open(path)?;\n        f.seek(SeekFrom::Start(offset))?;\n        f.write_all(data)?;\n        f.sync_all()\n    }\n\n    fn truncate(&self, path: &Path, len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let f = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).open(path)?;\n        f.set_len(len)?;\n        f.sync_all()\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let f = std::fs::OpenOptions::new().write(true).open(path)?;\n        f.sync_all()\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// In-memory filesystem.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[derive(Default)]\nstruct MemInner {\n    files: BTreeMap<PathBuf, Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone, Default)]\npub struct MemVfs {\n    inner: Arc<Mutex<MemInner>>,\n}\n\nimpl MemVfs {\n    pub fn new() -> Self {\n        Self::default()\n    }\n\n    /// Test helper: raw snapshot of a file (or an empty buffer if absent).\n    pub fn snapshot(&self, path: &Path) -> Vec<u8> {\n        self.inner\n            .lock()\n            .unwrap()\n            .files\n            .get(path)\n            .cloned()\n            .unwrap_or_default()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Vfs for MemVfs {\n    fn exists(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<bool> {\n        Ok(self.inner.lock().unwrap().files.contains_key(path))\n    }\n\n    fn read(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {\n        match self.inner.lock().unwrap().files.get(path) {\n            Some(d) => Ok(d.clone()),\n            None => Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, \"memfs: no such file\")),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn write_atomic(&self, path: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        g.files.insert(path.to_path_buf(), data.to_vec());\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn remove(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        match g.files.remove(path) {\n            Some(_) => Ok(()),\n            None => Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, \"memfs: no such file\")),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn len(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<u64> {\n        match self.inner.lock().unwrap().files.get(path) {\n            Some(d) => Ok(d.len() as u64),\n            None => Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, \"memfs: no such file\")),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn read_at(&self, path: &Path, offset: u64, buf: &mut [u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {\n        let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        match g.files.get(path) {\n            Some(d) => {\n                let off = offset as usize;\n                if off >= d.len() {\n                    return Ok(0);\n                }\n                let n = buf.len().min(d.len() - off);\n                buf[..n].copy_from_slice(&d[off..off + n]);\n                Ok(n)\n            }\n            None => Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, \"memfs: no such file\")),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn write_at(&self, path: &Path, offset: u64, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let entry = g.files.entry(path.to_path_buf()).or_default();\n        let end = offset as usize + data.len();\n        if end > entry.len() {\n            entry.resize(end, 0);\n        }\n        entry[offset as usize..end].copy_from_slice(data);\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn truncate(&self, path: &Path, len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        match g.files.get_mut(path) {\n            Some(d) => {\n                d.resize(len as usize, 0);\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            None => Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::NotFound, \"memfs: no such file\")),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn sync(&self, _path: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Fault-injecting wrapper.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Op {\n    Exists,\n    Read,\n    WriteAtomic,\n    Remove,\n    Len,\n    ReadAt,\n    WriteAt,\n    Truncate,\n    Sync,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nenum Effect {\n    /// Fail the nth matching call with an io::Error.\n    Fail(u64),\n    /// Flip the first byte written by the nth matching call (torn write).\n    Corrupt(u64),\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone)]\nstruct Rule {\n    op: Op,\n    path_contains: Option<String>,\n    effect: Effect,\n    fired: bool,\n}\n\n/// Wraps a [`Vfs`]; each rule fires at most once. Typical test use:\n/// `FaultyVfs::new(inner).fail_on(Op::WriteAtomic, Some(\"manifest\"), 3)`.\npub struct FaultyVfs<V: Vfs> {\n    inner: V,\n    rules: Mutex<Vec<Rule>>,\n    counters: Mutex<BTreeMap<(Op, String), u64>>,\n}\n\nimpl<V: Vfs> FaultyVfs<V> {\n    pub fn new(inner: V) -> Self {\n        FaultyVfs {\n            inner,\n            rules: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),\n tmp.set_file_name(format!(\".{}.tmp-{}\", file_name.to_string_lossy(), std::process::id()));\n        {\n            let mut f = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n                .write(true)\n
