{"parentUuid":"887ab521-e263-4c73-bf52-fb8da2287246","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_b1gjf2f4gkogv20eq3ej81lf","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp10/a/src/api.rs","content":"//! HTTP API handlers and the repository-independent verification endpoint.\n\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\nuse crate::base64;\nuse crate::http::{Handler, Request, Response};\nuse crate::json::{self, Json};\nuse crate::merkle::{self, RangeProof};\nuse crate::store::{Store, StoreError};\nuse crate::vfs::RealVfs;\n\npub fn hex(h: &[u8]) -> String {\n    h.iter().map(|b| format!(\"{b:02x}\")).collect()\n}\n\nfn root_fields(root: &merkle::Hash32) -> Vec<(&'static str, Json)> {\n    vec![\n        (\"root\", Json::Str(base64::encode(root))),\n        (\"root_hex\", Json::Str(hex(root))),\n    ]\n}\n\npub struct RepoHandler {\n    store: Mutex<Store<RealVfs>>,\n}\n\nimpl RepoHandler {\n    pub fn new(store: Store<RealVfs>) -> Self {\n        RepoHandler {\n            store: Mutex::new(store),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn open(dir: &Path) -> Result<Self, StoreError> {\n        Ok(Self::new(Store::open(RealVfs::new(), dir)?))\n    }\n\n    pub fn shared(store: Store<RealVfs>) -> Arc<Self> {\n        Arc::new(Self::new(store))\n    }\n}\n\nfn store_err_response(e: StoreError) -> Response {\n    match e {\n        StoreError::InvalidInput(msg) => Response::error_json(400, &msg),\n        StoreError::Corrupt(msg) => Response::error_json(500, &msg),\n        StoreError::Io(io) => Response::error_json(500, &format!(\"io error: {io}\")),\n    }\n}\n\nfn parse_u64(s: Option<String>, name: &str) -> Result<u64, Response> {\n    s.and_then(|v| v.parse().ok())\n        .ok_or_else(|| Response::error_json(400, &format!(\"missing/invalid '{name}'\")))\n}\n\nimpl Handler for RepoHandler {\n    fn handle(&self, req: &Request) -> Response {\n        match (req.method.as_str(), req.path.as_str()) {\n            (\"GET\", \"/health\") => Response::json(\n                200,\n                json::obj(vec![(\"status\", Json::Str(\"ok\".into()))]).pretty(),\n            ),\n            (\"GET\", \"/\") => Response::json(\n                200,\n                json::obj(vec![\n                    (\"service\", Json::Str(\"merkle-store\".into())),\n                    (\n                        \"endpoints\",\n                        Json::Array(\n                            [\n                                \"GET /health\",\n                                \"GET /root\",\n                                \"GET /range?start=0&end=1 (or which=first|last)\",\n                                \"PUT /block?index=0 (raw bytes)\",\n                                \"POST /build (raw bytes; full-file atomic build)\",\n                                \"POST /verify (self-contained JSON, does not touch the store)\",\n                            ]\n                            .iter()\n                            .map(|s| Json::Str((*s).to_string()))\n                            .collect(),\n                        ),\n                    ),\n                ])\n                .pretty(),\n            ),\n            (\"GET\", \"/root\") => self.handle_root(),\n            (\"GET\", \"/range\") => self.handle_range(req),\n            (\"PUT\", \"/block\") => self.handle_put_block(req),\n            (\"POST\", \"/build\") => self.handle_build(req),\n            (\"POST\", \"/verify\") => verify_request(req),\n            (_, _) => Response::error_json(404, \"no such endpoint\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl RepoHandler {\n    fn handle_root(&self) -> Response {\n        let s = self.store.lock().unwrap();\n        match s.root() {\n            Ok(r) => {\n                let mut fields = vec![\n                    (\"block_size\", Json::Int(s.block_size() as i64)),\n                    (\"data_len\", Json::Int(s.data_len() as i64)),\n                    (\"n\", Json::Int(s.block_count() as i64)),\n                ];\n                fields.extend(root_fields(&r));\n                Response::json(200, json::obj(fields).pretty())\n            }\n            Err(e) => store_err_response(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn handle_range(&self, req: &Request) -> Response {\n        let (start, end) = match resolve_range(req) {\n            Ok(v) => v,\n            Err(r) => return r,\n        };\n        let s = self.store.lock().unwrap();\n        let proof = match s.prove_range(start, end) {\n            Ok(p) => p,\n            Err(e) => return store_err_response(e),\n        };\n        let mut blocks = Vec::new();\n        for i in start..end {\n            match s.read_block(i) {\n                Ok(bytes) => blocks.push(Json::obj(vec![\n                    (\"index\", Json::Int(i as i64)),\n                    (\"length\", Json::Int(bytes.len() as i64)),\n                    (\"data\", Json::Str(base64::encode(&bytes))),\n                ])),\n                Err(e) => return store_err_response(e),\n            }\n        }\n        match s.root() {\n            Ok(root) => {\n                let mut fields = vec![\n                    (\"block_size\", Json::Int(s.block_size() as i64)),\n                    (\"data_len\", Json::Int(s.data_len() as i64)),\n                    (\"n\", Json::Int(s.block_count() as i64)),\n                    (\"start\", Json::Int(start as i64)),\n                    (\"end\", Json::Int(end as i64)),\n                    (\"blocks\", Json::Array(blocks)),\n                    (\"proof\", merkle::proof_to_json(&proof)),\n                ];\n                fields.extend(root_fields(&root));\n                Response::json(200, json::obj(fields).pretty())\n            }\n            Err(e) => store_err_response(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn handle_put_block(&self, req: &Request) -> Response {\n        let index = match parse_u64(req.query_param(\"index\"), \"index\") {\n            Ok(v) => v,\n            Err(r) => return r,\n        };\n        let mut s = self.store.lock().unwrap();\n        if let Err(e) = s.put_block(index, &req.body) {\n            return store_err_response(e);\n        }\n        match s.root() {\n            Ok(r) => {\n                let mut fields = vec![\n                    (\"ok\", Json::Bool(true)),\n                    (\"index\", Json::Int(index as i64)),\n                    (\"data_len\", Json::Int(s.data_len() as i64)),\n                    (\"n\", Json::Int(s.block_count() as i64)),\n                ];\n                fields.extend(root_fields(&r));\n                Response::json(200, json::obj(fields).pretty())\n            }\n            Err(e) => store_err_response(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn handle_build(&self, req: &Request) -> Response {\n        let mut s = self.store.lock().unwrap();\n        if let Err(e) = s.reset(&req.body) {\n            return store_err_response(e);\n        }\n        match s.root() {\n            Ok(r) => {\n                let mut fields = vec![\n                    (\"ok\", Json::Bool(true)),\n                    (\"data_len\", Json::Int(s.data_len() as i64)),\n                    (\"n\", Json::Int(s.block_count() as i64)),\n                ];\n                fields.extend(root_fields(&r));\n                Response::json(200, json::obj(fields).pretty())\n            }\n            Err(e) => store_err_response(e),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn resolve_range(req: &Request) -> Result<(u64, u64), Response> {\n    // Resolve against the store: which=first|last convenience aliases.\n    // We need n, which the caller handler knows; simplest is to read params\n    // and let the handler validate — but n lives behind the lock. Parse here\n    // and return sentinel aliases for the handler to map.\n    if let Some(which) = req.query_param(\"which\") {\n        return match which.as_str() {\n            \"first\" => Ok((u64::MAX - 1, u64::MAX - 1)),\n            \"last\" => Ok((u64::MAX - 2, u64::MAX - 2)),\n            _ => Err(Response::error_json(400, \"which must be first|last\")),\n        };\n    }\n    let start = parse_u64(req.query_param(\"start\"), \"start\")?;\n    let end = parse_u64(req.query_param(\"end\"), \"end\")?;\n    Ok((start, end))\n}\n\n/// Stateless verification: the request carries everything the verifier needs\n/// (trusted root, declared sizes, block bytes, proof). The store is never read.\npub fn verify_request(req: &Request) -> Response {\n    verify_body(&req.body)\n}\n\npub fn verify_body(body: &[u8]) -> Response {\n    let parsed = match json::parse(&String::from_utf8_lossy(body)) {\n        Ok(v) => v,\n        Err(e) => return Response::error_json(400, &format!(\"invalid JSON: {e}\")),\n    };\n    match verify_parsed(&parsed) {\n        Ok(()) => Response::json(\n            200,\n            json::obj(vec![(\"valid\", Json::Bool(true))]).pretty(),\n        ),\n        Err(msg) => Response::json(\n            200,\n            json::obj(vec![\n                (\"valid\", Json::Bool(false)),\n                (\"error\", Json::Str(msg)),\n            ])\n            .pretty(),\n        ),\n    }\n}\n\nfn field_i64(v: &Json, name: &str) -> Result<i64, String> {\n    v.get(name)\n        .and_then(Json::as_i64)\n        .ok_or_else(|| format!(\"missing/invalid '{name}'\"))\n}\n\nfn verify_parsed(v: &Json) -> Result<(), String> {\n    let block_size = field_i64(v, \"block_size\")?;\n    let data_len = field_i64(v, \"data_len\")?;\n    let n = field_i64(v, \"n\")?;\n    let start = field_i64(v, \"start\")?;\n    let end = field_i64(v, \"end\")?;\n    if block_size <= 0 || data_len < 0 || n < 0 || start < 0 || end < 0 {\n        return Err(\"numeric fields must be non-negative (block_size > 0)\".into());\n    }\n\n    let root_s = v\n        .get(\"root\")\n        .and_then(Json::as_str)\n        .ok_or(\"missing 'root' (base64 of 32 bytes)\")?;\n    let root_bytes = base64::decode(root_s).map_err(|_| \"root not valid base64\".to_string())?;\n    if root_bytes.len() != 32 {\n        return Err(\"root must decode to 32 bytes\".into());\n    }\n    let mut root = [0u8; 32];\n    root.copy_from_slice(&root_bytes);\n\n    let blocks_v = v\n        .get(\"blocks\")\n        .and_then(Json::as_array)\n        .ok_or(\"missing 'blocks' array\")?;\n    let mut blocks = Vec::with_capacity(blocks_v.len());\n    for item in blocks_v {\n        let s = item\n            .as_str()\n            .ok_or(\"blocks must be base64 strings\")?;\n        blocks.push(base64::decode(s).map_err(|_| \"block not valid base64\")?);\n    }\n\n    let proof: RangeProof = merkle::proof_from_json(\n        n as usize,\n        start as usize,\n        end as usize,\n        v.get(\"proof\").ok_or(\"missing 'proof' array\")?,\n    )?;\n\n    merkle::verify(\n        &proof,\n        block_size as u64,\n        data_len as u64,\n        &root,\n        &blocks,\n    )\n    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_5eb3dccb40bb0ba8d40e69cb","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":2725,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":83768,"output_tokens":3659,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_b1gjf2f4gkogv20eq3ej81lf":{"content":"//! {"parentUuid":"2c953682-1123-458c-af3c-511d873beefd","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_64nbkfhbuobicpuafjzz09pm","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp10/a/src/main.rs","content":"//! `merkle-store` CLI: local server, raw HTTP client, and offline verifier.\n\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::TcpStream;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::process::ExitCode;\n\nuse merkle_store::api::{self, RepoHandler};\nuse merkle_store::base64;\nuse merkle_store::http;\nuse merkle_store::json::{self, Json};\nuse merkle_store::merkle;\nuse merkle_store::store::Store;\nuse merkle_store::vfs::RealVfs;\n\nfn usage() -> String {\n    r#\"merkle-store — incremental Merkle-verified block store\n\nUSAGE:\n  merkle-store init  <dir> --block-size <N>\n  merkle-store build <dir> --file <path> [--block-size <N>]   (block-size only used for init)\n  merkle-store put   <dir> --index <I> --file <path>\n  merkle-store root  <dir>\n  merkle-store range <dir> (--start <S> --end <E>) | --which first|last\n  merkle-store verify <request.json>          offline verify of a /range response + trusted root\n  merkle-store serve <dir> --addr 127.0.0.1:8080\n  merkle-store req   <addr> <METHOD> <path> [--data <file>]\n\nThe `verify` subcommand reads the JSON body of a GET /range response plus a\n\"root\" field (the trusted root, base64) and performs verification locally.\n\"#\n    .to_string()\n}\n\nfn arg(args: &[String], name: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    args.iter().position(|a| a == name).and_then(|i| args.get(i + 1)).cloned()\n}\n\nfn read_file(path: &str) -> std::io::Result<Vec<u8>> {\n    std::fs::read(path)\n}\n\nfn print_json(body: &[u8]) -> i32 {\n    match std::str::from_utf8(body) {\n        Ok(text) => match json::parse(text) {\n            Ok(v) => print!(\"{}\", v.pretty()),\n            Err(_) => print!(\"{text}\"),\n        },\n        Err(_) => print!(\"{}\", String::from_utf8_lossy(body)),\n    }\n    0\n}\n\nfn cmd_init(args: &[String]) -> ExitCode {\n    let dir = match args.first() {\n        Some(d) => d,\n        None => {\n            eprintln!(\"{}\", usage());\n            return ExitCode::from(2);\n        }\n    };\n    let bs = match arg(args, \"--block-size\").and_then(|s| s.parse::<u64>().ok()) {\n        Some(n) if n > 0 => n,\n        _ => {\n            eprintln!(\"--block-size <positive integer> required\");\n            return ExitCode::from(2);\n        }\n    };\n    match Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &PathBuf::from(dir), bs) {\n        Ok(_) => {\n            println!(\"initialized empty repository at {dir} (block_size={bs})\");\n            ExitCode::SUCCESS\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"error: {e}\");\n            ExitCode::FAILURE\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn cmd_build(args: &[String]) -> ExitCode {\n    let (dir, file) = match (args.first(), arg(args, \"--file\")) {\n        (Some(d), Some(f)) => (d, f),\n        _ => {\n            eprintln!(\"build <dir> --file <path>\");\n            return ExitCode::from(2);\n        }\n    };\n    let bytes = match read_file(&file) {\n        Ok(b) => b,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"cannot read {file}: {e}\");\n            return ExitCode::FAILURE;\n        }\n    };\n    let result = Store::open(RealVfs::new(), &PathBuf::from(dir))\n        .and_then(|mut s| s.reset(&bytes));\n .to_string()\n}\n\nfn arg(args: &[String], name: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    args.iter().position(|a| a == name).and_then(|i| args.get(i + 1)).cloned()\n}\n\nfn read_file(path: &str) -> bs = match arg(args, \"--block-size\").and_then(|s| s.parse::<u64>().ok()) {\n        Some(n) if n > 0 => n,\n        _ => {\n            eprintln!(\"--block-size <positive integer> required\");\n            return ExitCode::from(2);\n        }\n    };\n    match Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &PathBuf::from(dir), bs) {\n        Ok(_) => {\n            println!(\"initialized empty repository at {dir} (block_size={bs})\");\n            ExitCode::SUCCESS\n        }\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"error: {e}\");\n            ExitCode::FAILURE\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn cmd_build(args: &[String]) -> ExitCode {\n    let (dir, file) = match (args.first(), arg(args, \"--file\")) {\n        (Some(d), Some(f)) => (d, f),\n        _ => {\n            eprintln!(\"build <dir> --file <path>\");\n            return ExitCode::from(2);\n        }\n    };\n    let bytes = match read_file(&file) {\n        Ok(b) => b,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"cannot read {file}: {e}\");\n            return ExitCode::FAILURE;\n        }\n    };\n    let result = Store::open(RealVfs::new(), &PathBuf::from(dir))\n        .and_then(|mut s| s.reset(&bytes));\n    match result {\n        Ok(()) => ExitCode::SUCCESS,\n        Err(e) => {\n            eprintln!(\"error: {e}\");\n            ExitCode::FAILURE\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn cmd_put(args: &[String]) -> index, file) {\n        (Some(d), Some(i), Some(f)) => (d, i, f),\n        _ => {\n            eprintln!(\"put <dir> --index <I> --file <path>\");\n            return ExitCode::from(2);\n        }\n }\n}\n\nfn cmd_root(args: &[String]) -> ExitCode {\n    let dir = match args.first() {\n        Some(d) => d,\n        None => return ExitCode::from(2),\n    };\n    match Store::open(RealVfs::new(), if the fault landed after\n                // the commit, the write simply succeeds.\n                let _ = s.put_block(1, b\"ef\");\n            }\n            // Reopen on a clean wrapper over the SAME backing store.\n            let mut s = Store::open(inner.clone(), Path::new(\"/x\")).unwrap();\n            assert_eq!(s.read_data().unwrap(), b\"abcdef\", \"rule {rule}\");\n            assert_eq!(\n                s.root().unwrap(),\n                expected_root(b\"abcdef\", 4),\n                \"rule {rule}\"\n            );\n            // After recovery the store remains usable.\n            s.put_block(2, b\"gh\").unwrap();\n            assert_eq!(s.read_data().unwrap(), b\"abcdefgh\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn recover_torn_level_bytes() {\n        let inner = MemVfs::new();\n        {\n            // Corrupt the first level-0 patch of the append, journal survives.\n            let vfs = FaultyVfs::new(inner.clone())\n                .corrupt_on(Op::WriteAt, Some(\"level-0\"), 1);\n            let mut s = Store::create(vfs, Path::new(\"/y\"), 4).unwrap();\n            let _ = s.put_block(0, b\"abcd\");\n        }\n        let s = Store::open(inner.clone(), Path::new(\"/y\")).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(s.read_data().unwrap(), b\"abcd\");\n        assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), expected_root(b\"abcd\", 4));\n    }","new_string":"        // Append a second block, failing the nth WriteAt/WriteAtomic call;\n        // every interrupted transaction must replay to the same final state.\n        // Call order per append: journal(A,1) data(W,2) level-0(W,3)\n        // level-1(W,4) manifest(A,5). Rule 1 means \"crash\" right after the\n        // journal landed — data untouched, replay still yields the append.\n        for rule in 1u64..=5 {\n            let inner = fresh_inner();\n            {\n                let vfs = FaultyVfs::new(inner.clone()).fail_on(Op::WriteAtomic, None, rule)\n                    .fail_on(Op::WriteAt, None, rule);\n                let mut s = Store::open(vfs, Path::new(\"/x\")).unwrap();\n                // An injected error is expected here; if the fault landed after\n                // the commit, the write simply succeeds.\n                let _ = s.put_block(1, b\"ef\");\n            }\n            // Reopen on a clean wrapper over the SAME backing store.\n            let mut s = Store::open(inner.clone(), Path::new(\"/x\")).unwrap();\n            assert_eq!(s.read_data().unwrap(), b\"abcdef\", \"rule {rule}\");\n            assert_eq!(\n                s.root().unwrap(),\n                expected_root(b\"abcdef\", 4),\n                \"rule {rule}\"\n            );\n            // After recovery the store remains usable.\n            s.put_block(2, b\"gh\").unwrap();\n            assert_eq!(s.read_data().unwrap(), b\"abcdefgh\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn recover_torn_level_bytes() {\n        let inner = MemVfs::new();\n        {\n            // Flip a level-0 byte (torn write) AND make the manifest publish\n            // fail, so the journal survives and forces a full rebuild.\n            let vfs = FaultyVfs::new(inner.clone())\n                .corrupt_on(Op::WriteAt, Some(\"level-0\"), 1)\n                .fail_on(Op::WriteAtomic, Some(\"manifest\"), 1);\n            let mut s = Store::create(vfs, Path::new(\"/y\"), 4).unwrap();\n            let _ = s.put_block(0, b\"abcd\");\n        }\n        let s = Store::open(inner.clone(), Path::new(\"/y\")).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(s.read_data().unwrap(), b\"abcd\");\n        assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), expected_root(b\"abcd\", 4));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn silent_level_corruption_without_journal_is_detected() {\n        // If level bytes are torn but the transaction committed (journal\n        // removed), the on-disk root no longer matches the data. force_full_rebuild\n        // recomputes it from data.bin; if the fault landed after\n                // the commit, the write simply succeeds.\n                let _ = s.put_block(1, b\"ef\");\n            }\n            // Reopen on a clean wrapper over the SAME backing store.\n            let mut s = Store::open(inner.clone(), Path::new(\"/x\")).unwrap();\n            assert_eq!(s.read_data().unwrap(), b\"abcdef\", \"rule {rule}\");\n            assert_eq!(\n                s.root().unwrap(),\n                expected_root(b\"abcdef\", 4),\n                \"rule {rule}\"\n            );\n            // After recovery the store remains usable.\n            s.put_block(2, b\"gh\").unwrap();\n            assert_eq!(s.read_data().unwrap(), b\"abcdefgh\");\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn recover_torn_level_bytes() {\n        let inner = MemVfs::new();\n        {\n            // Flip a level-0 byte (torn write) AND make the manifest publish\n            // fail, so the journal survives and forces a full rebuild.\n            let vfs = FaultyVfs::new(inner.clone())\n                .corrupt_on(Op::WriteAt, Some(\"level-0\"), 1)\n                .fail_on(Op::WriteAtomic, Some(\"manifest\"), 1);\n            let mut s = Store::create(vfs, Path::new(\"/y\"), 4).unwrap();\n            let _ = s.put_block(0, b\"abcd\");\n        }\n        let s = Store::open(inner.clone(), Path::new(\"/y\")).unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(s.read_data().unwrap(), b\"abcd\");\n        assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), expected_root(b\"abcd\", 4));\n    }","new_string":"        // Append a second block, failing the nth mutating VFS call; {"parentUuid":"489a8d93-ba6f-44c9-b9d0-30c766724301","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"signature":"","thinking":"The single overwrite test passes. \n\nI've confirmed the root cause of the issue: my test incorrectly applies file truncation logic to all non-last blocks during overwrites, instead of only doing so for the last block, leading to the accumulation bug.\n\nI've further identified another truncation bug in the store module: the unconditionally applied truncation logic will incorrectly shrink the file when writing to non-last blocks.\n\nI've verified this truncation bug can cause severe issues: overwriting a non-last block will accidentally delete subsequent data, corrupting the stored root hash and leading to manifest decoding failures on the next database opening. I've also worked out the fix: add an is_last flag to identify the written block, only trigger truncation for short writes to the last block, and adjust the store's put logic accordingly.\n\nI've refined the fix details: adjust the signature of the apply_put_to_data function. For the live path, only trigger truncation when writing to the last existing block, and disable truncation for appends. For `reset` there is one leading entry carrying the whole new payload and\n32\t//! n = ceil(len/block_size). `put` entries may append or overwrite one block.\n33\t//!\n34\t//! ## Sync boundary per mutating request\n35\t//! 1. Journal written atomically (temp+fsync+rename+dir fsync).\n36\t//! 2. `data.bin` patched (pwrite + fsync) — truncate when needed.\n37\t//! 3. Affected Merkle levels patched incrementally (pwrite + fsync each).\n38\t//! 4. New manifest published atomically; journal deleted; directory fsynced.\n39\t//!\n40\t//! A manifest is published only via temp-file + fsync + rename + dir fsync, so\n25\t//! a 64-byte file is either the previous or the new manifest, never torn.\n26\t//!\n27\t//! ### journal\n28\t//! | magic `MS-JOURNAL-V1\\0\\0\\0` (16) |\n29\t//! repeated entries:\n30\t//! | op:u8 = 1 put / 2 reset | index:u64 | len:u64 | data(len) |\n31\t//! For `reset` there is one leading entry carrying the whole new payload and\n32\t//! n = ceil(len/block_size). `put` entries may append or overwrite one block.\n33\t//!\n34\t//! ## Sync boundary per mutating request\n35\t//! 1. Journal written atomically (temp+fsync+rename+dir fsync).\n36\t//! 2. `data.bin` patched (pwrite + fsync) — truncate when needed.\n37\t//! 3. Affected Merkle levels patched incrementally (pwrite + fsync each).\n38\t//! 4. New manifest published atomically; journal deleted; directory fsynced.\n39\t//!\n40\t//! Crash between 1 and 4 is repaired on next open by replaying the journal\n41\t//! against `data.bin` and fully rebuilding every level file — always safe\n42\t//! whether or not some level bytes had already been patched.\n43\t\n44\tuse std::io;\n45\tuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n46\t\n47\tuse crate::merkle::{\n48\t    self, build_levels, empty_root, internal_hash, leaf_hash, Hash32,  InvalidInput(String),\n64\t}\n65\t\n66\timpl std::fmt::Display for StoreError {\n67\t    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n68\t        match self {\n69\t {\n80\t        StoreError::Io(e)\n81\t    }\n82\t}\n83\t\n84\ttype Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, StoreError>;\n85\t\n86\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n87\tpub struct Manifest {\n88\t {"parentUuid":"8b5b30cf-f22e-4f96-bf29-45c2facd364d","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_5cxjp7a92fomzj2hnjcnyjv7","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp10/a/tests/acceptance.rs","content":"//! Acceptance criteria, exercised against the real on-disk repository.\n//!\n//! Covers:\n//! - incremental root equals a full rebuild root;\n//! - first/last range proofs verify, verifier reads no other blocks;\n//! - empty file;\n//! - forged length;\n//! - displaced/misaligned proof nodes;\n//! - incremental update touches only O(height) level nodes;\n//! - crash recovery through every journaled step on a real filesystem.\n\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse merkle_store::merkle::{\n    self, empty_root, leaf_hash, ProofError, ProofNode, RangeProof,\n};\nuse merkle_store::store::Store;\nuse merkle_store::vfs::{FaultyVfs, Op, RealVfs};\n\nfn full_rebuild_root(data: &[u8], bs: u64) -> [u8; 32] {\n    let leaves: Vec<[u8; 32]> = data\n        .chunks(bs as usize)\n        .enumerate()\n        .map(|(i, c)| leaf_hash(i, c))\n        .collect();\n    merkle::rebuild_root(&leaves)\n}\n\nfn tempdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    let mut d = std::env::temp_dir();\n    let unique = format!(\n        \"merkle-store-it-{}-{}-{}\",\n        tag,\n        std::process::id(),\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .unwrap()\n            .as_nanos()\n    );\n    d.push(unique);\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&d).unwrap();\n    d\n}\n\nfn open_real(dir: &Path) -> Store<RealVfs> {\n    Store::open(RealVfs::new(), dir).unwrap()\n}\n\n// 1. Incremental root == full rebuild root -------------------------------\n\n#[test]\nfn incremental_matches_full_rebuild_after_mixed_updates() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"incr\");\n    let bs = 7u64;\n    let mut s = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, bs).unwrap();\n\n    let payload: Vec<u8> = (0..137u32).map(|i| (i % 251) as u8).collect();\n    let mut expected = Vec::new();\n    for (i, chunk) in payload.chunks(bs as usize).enumerate() {\n        s.put_block(i as u64, chunk).unwrap();\n        expected.extend_from_slice(chunk);\n        assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), full_rebuild_root(&expected, bs));\n    }\n\n    // Overwrite the first, a middle, and the last block.\n    let overwrite = |s: &mut Store<RealVfs>, expected: &mut Vec<u8>, i: usize, bytes: &[u8]| {\n        s.put_block(i as u64, bytes).unwrap();\n        let start = i * bs as usize;\n        if start + bytes.len() < expected.len() {\n            expected.truncate(start + bytes.len());\n        }\n        expected[start..start + bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(bytes);\n        assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), full_rebuild_root(expected, bs));\n    };\n    overwrite(&mut s, &mut expected, 0, b\"ZZZZZZZ\");\n    overwrite(&mut s, &mut expected, 10, b\"middle!\");\n    let n = expected.len().div_ceil(bs as usize);\n    overwrite(&mut s, &mut expected, n - 1, b\"tail\"); // shortens last block\n\n    // Independent verification path: force a full rebuild and compare roots.\n    let committed = s.root().unwrap();\n    s.force_full_rebuild().unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), committed);\n    assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), full_rebuild_root(&expected, bs));\n}\n\n// 2. First / last range proofs -------------------------------------------\n\n#[test]\nfn first_and_last_range_proofs_verify_without_reading_other_blocks() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"ranges\");\n    let bs = 4u64;\n    let data = b\"the quick brown fox jumps over\"; // 31 bytes -> 8 blocks\n    let mut s = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, bs).unwrap();\n    s.reset(data).unwrap();\n    let root = s.root().unwrap();\n    let n = s.block_count();\n\n    for (st, en) in [(0u64, 1u64), (n - 1, n)] {\n        let proof = s.prove_range(st, en).unwrap();\n        // The verifier is given ONLY the requested block bytes.\n        let blocks: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (st..en).map(|i| s.read_block(i).unwrap()).collect();\n        merkle::verify(&proof, bs, data.len() as u64, &root, &blocks).unwrap();\n    }\n\n    // A multi-block interior range also verifies.\n    let proof = s.prove_range(2, 6).unwrap();\n    let blocks: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (2..6).map(|i| s.read_block(i).unwrap()).collect();\n    merkle::verify(&proof, bs, data.len() as u64, &root, &blocks).unwrap();\n\n    // The last block is the short one (31 -> last block length 3).\n    let last = s.read_block(n - 1).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(last.len(), 3);\n}\n\n// 3. Empty file ------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[test]\nfn empty_file_has_sentinel_root_and_verifies() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"empty\");\n    let s = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, 16).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(s.block_count(), 0);\n    assert_eq!(s.data_len(), 0);\n    assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), empty_root());\n\n    // The canonical empty proof: range [0,0), no nodes, against the sentinel.\n    let proof = RangeProof { n: 0, start: 0, end: 0, nodes: vec![] };\n    merkle::verify(&proof, 16, 0, &empty_root(), &[]).unwrap();\n\n    // Empty proof against a non-empty root must fail.\n    assert_eq!(\n        merkle::verify(&proof, 16, 0, &[1u8; 32], &[]).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::EmptyRootMismatch\n    );\n\n    // Building data then resetting to empty restores the sentinel.\n    let dir2 = tempdir(\"empty2\");\n    let mut s2 = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir2, 16).unwrap();\n    s2.reset(b\"hello\").unwrap();\n    assert_ne!(s2.root().unwrap(), empty_root());\n    s2.reset(b\"\").unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(s2.root().unwrap(), empty_root());\n}\n\n// 4. Forged length ---------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[test]\nfn forged_length_is_rejected() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"forgelen\");\n    let bs = 4u64;\n    let data = b\"abcde\";\n    let mut s = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, bs).unwrap();\n    s.reset(data).unwrap();\n    let root = s.root().unwrap();\n\n    // Honest last-block proof (block 2, one byte).\n    let proof = s.prove_range(2, 3).unwrap();\n    let good = vec![b\"e\".to_vec()];\n    merkle::verify(&proof, bs, 5, &root, &good).unwrap();\n\n    // 4a. Declared length that implies a different leaf count.\n    assert_eq!(\n        merkle::verify(&proof, bs, 8, &root, &good).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::LengthMismatch\n    );\n    assert_eq!(\n        merkle::verify(&proof, bs, 4, &root, &good).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::LengthMismatch\n    );\n\n    // 4b. Padding the short last block to full size is caught at the leaf.\n    assert!(matches!(\n        merkle::verify(&proof, bs, 8, &root, &[b\"e\\0\\0\\0\".to_vec()]).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::LengthMismatch | ProofError::LeafMismatch { .. }\n    ));\n\n    // 4c. Wrong trusted root with an otherwise valid proof.\n    assert_eq!(\n        merkle::verify(&proof, bs, 5, &[0u8; 32], &good).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::RootMismatch\n    );\n}\n\n// 5. Displaced / misaligned proofs ----------------------------------------\n\n#[test]\nfn misaligned_proofs_are_rejected() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"misalign\");\n    let bs = 4u64;\n    let data = b\"abcdefghijkl\"; // 12 bytes, 3 blocks\n    let mut s = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, bs).unwrap();\n    s.reset(data).unwrap();\n    let root = s.root().unwrap();\n    let good = s.prove_range(1, 2).unwrap();\n    let blocks = vec![b\"efgh\".to_vec()];\n    merkle::verify(&good, bs, 12, &root, &blocks).unwrap();\n\n    // 5a. Swap sibling nodes.\n    let mut p = good.clone();\n    p.nodes.swap(1, 2);\n    assert!(matches!(\n        merkle::verify(&p, bs, 12, &root, &blocks).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::MisalignedNode { .. }\n    ));\n\n    // 5b. Retag a node to the wrong index.\n    let mut p = good.clone();\n    p.nodes[1].index = 5;\n    assert!(matches!(\n        merkle::verify(&p, bs, 12, &root, &blocks).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::MisalignedNode { .. }\n    ));\n\n    // 5c. Truncated / extended proofs.\n    let mut p = good.clone();\n    p.nodes.pop();\n    assert_eq!(\n        merkle::verify(&p, bs, 12, &root, &blocks).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::ProofTooShort\n    );\n    let mut p = good.clone();\n    p.nodes.push(ProofNode { level: 3, index: 3, hash: [9u8; 32] });\n    assert_eq!(\n        merkle::verify(&p, bs, 12, &root, &blocks).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::ProofTooLong\n    );\n\n    // 5d. Present a proof generated for a different file length.\n    let mut s2 = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &tempdir(\"misalign2\"), bs).unwrap();\n    s2.reset(b\"abcdefghijklm\").unwrap(); // 13 bytes, still 4? no -> 4 blocks\n    let foreign = s2.prove_range(1, 2).unwrap();\n    // The foreign proof's tree shape may still structurally verify up to a\n    // different root; it must at minimum fail the root binding.\n    let err = merkle::verify(&foreign, bs, 12, &root, &blocks).unwrap_err();\n    assert!(\n        matches!(\n            err,\n            ProofError::RootMismatch\n                | ProofError::LengthMismatch\n                | ProofError::MisalignedNode { .. }\n                | ProofError::ProofTooShort\n                | ProofError::LeafMismatch { .. }\n        ),\n        \"unexpected acceptance of foreign proof: {err:?}\"\n    );\n}\n\n// 6. Incremental update cost ----------------------------------------------\n\n#[test]\nfn incremental_update_writes_only_one_path() {\n    use merkle_store::vfs::Vfs;\n    let inner = merkle_store::vfs::MemVfs::new();\n    let bs = 1u64;\n    // Build a 256-leaf tree via a full reset.\n    {\n        let mut s = Store::create(inner.clone(), Path::new(\"/cost\"), bs).unwrap();\n        let data: Vec<u8> = (0..256u16).map(|i| i as u8).collect();\n        s.reset(&data).unwrap();\n    }\n    // Overwrite a single leaf on an instrumented VFS.\n    let vfs = FaultyVfs::new(inner.clone());\n    let mut s = Store::open(vfs.clone(), Path::new(\"/cost\")).unwrap();\n    s.put_block(100, &[0xAB]).unwrap();\n\n    // Exactly one 32-byte write per tree level on the affected path; the\n    // tree has 256 leaves -> 9 levels (0..=8).\n    let mut level_writes = 0u64;\n    for lvl in 0..16 {\n        let path = format!(\"level-{lvl}.bin\");\n        let n = vfs.call_count(Op::WriteAt, &path);\n        level_writes += n;\n        if lvl <= 8 {\n            assert_eq!(n, 1, \"expected exactly one write to {path}\");\n        } else {\n            assert_eq!(n, 0, \"no level {lvl} file should exist\");\n        }\n    }\n    assert_eq!(level_writes, 9, \"one node per level on the path\");\n    // data.bin gets exactly one pwrite as well.\n    assert_eq!(vfs.call_count(Op::WriteAt, \"data.bin\"), 1);\n}\n\n// 7. Crash recovery through every journaled step on a real filesystem ------\n\n#[test]\nfn real_fs_crash_replay_at_every_step() {\n    // Two-block append; instrumented writes fail at call N. After reopen the\n    // repository is internally consistent (root matches a full rebuild).\n    for rule in 1u64..=5 {\n        let dir = tempdir(&format!(\"crash-{rule}\"));\n        {\n            let mut base = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, 4).unwrap();\n            base.put_block(0, b\"abcd\").unwrap();\n        }\n        {\n            let vfs = FaultyVfs::new(RealVfs::new())\n                .fail_on(Op::WriteAtomic, None, rule)\n                .fail_on(Op::WriteAt, None, rule);\n            let mut s = Store::open(vfs, &dir).unwrap();\n            let _ = s.put_block(1, b\"efgh\");\n        }\n        let mut s = open_real(&dir);\n        let data = s.read_data().unwrap();\n        let root = s.root().unwrap();\n        // Whatever survived, the committed root must equal a full rebuild of\n        // exactly the bytes present in data.bin.\n        assert_eq!(root, full_rebuild_root(&data, 4), \"rule {rule}\");\n        assert!(data == b\"abcd\" || data == b\"abcdefgh\", \"rule {rule}: {data:?}\");\n        // The store is usable after recovery.\n        s.force_full_rebuild().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), full_rebuild_root(&data, 4));\n    }\n}\n\n// 8. Cross-check verifier against the store over many shapes --------------\n\n#[test]\nfn exhaustive_range_verification_small_trees() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"exhaustive\");\n    for bs in 1u64..=5 {\n        for nblocks in 0usize..10 {\n            let mut d = tempdir(&format!(\"ex-{bs}-{nblocks}\"));\n            let payload: Vec<u8> = (0..(nblocks as u64 * bs)).map(|i| (i % 199) as u8).collect();\n            let mut s = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &d, bs).unwrap();\n            s.reset(&payload).unwrap();\n            let root = s.root().unwrap();\n            if nblocks == 0 {\n                let p = s.prove_range(0, 0).unwrap();\n                merkle::verify(&p, bs, 0, &root, &[]).unwrap();\n                continue;\n            }\n            for st in 0..nblocks {\n                for en in st + 1..=nblocks {\n                    let p = s.prove_range(st as u64, en as u64).unwrap();\n                    let blocks: Vec<Vec<u8>> =\n                        (st..en).map(|i| s.read_block(i as u64).unwrap()).collect();\n                    merkle::verify(&p, bs, payload.len() as u64, &root, &blocks)\n                        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!(\"bs={bs} n={nblocks} {st}..{en}: {e}\"));\n                }\n            }\n            // silence unused mut on platforms\n            let _ = &mut d;\n        }\n    }\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_cff6c1b3385e61cda59bc7e6","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":965,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":135992,"output_tokens":4129,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_5cxjp7a92fomzj2hnjcnyjv7":{"content":"//! Incremental root == full rebuild root -------------------------------\n\n#[test]\nfn incremental_matches_full_rebuild_after_mixed_updates() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"incr\");\n    let bs = 7u64;\n    let mut s = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, bs).unwrap();\n\n    let payload: Vec<u8> = (0..137u32).map(|i| (i % 251) as u8).collect();\n    let mut expected = Vec::new();\n    for (i, chunk) in payload.chunks(bs as usize).enumerate() {\n        s.put_block(i as u64, chunk).unwrap();\n        expected.extend_from_slice(chunk);\n        assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), full_rebuild_root(&expected, bs));\n    }\n\n    // Overwrite the first, a middle, and the last block.\n    let overwrite = |s: &mut Store<RealVfs>, expected: &mut Vec<u8>, i: usize, bytes: &[u8]| {\n        s.put_block(i as u64, bytes).unwrap();\n        let start = i * bs as usize;\n        if start + bytes.len() < expected.len() {\n            expected.truncate(start + bytes.len());\n        }\n        expected[start..start + bytes.len()].copy_from_slice(bytes);\n        assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), full_rebuild_root(expected, bs));\n    };\n    overwrite(&mut s, &mut expected, 0, b\"ZZZZZZZ\");\n    overwrite(&mut s, &mut expected, 10, b\"middle!\");\n    let n = expected.len().div_ceil(bs as usize);\n    overwrite(&mut s, &mut expected, n - 1, b\"tail\"); // shortens last block\n\n    // Independent verification path: force a full rebuild and compare roots.\n    let committed = s.root().unwrap();\n    s.force_full_rebuild().unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), committed);\n    assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), full_rebuild_root(&expected, bs));\n}\n\n// 2. First / last range proofs -------------------------------------------\n\n#[test]\nfn first_and_last_range_proofs_verify_without_reading_other_blocks() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"ranges\");\n    let bs = 4u64;\n    let data = b\"the quick brown fox jumps over\"; // 31 bytes -> 8 blocks\n    let mut s = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, bs).unwrap();\n    s.reset(data).unwrap();\n    let root = s.root().unwrap();\n    let n = s.block_count();\n\n    for (st, en) in [(0u64, 1u64), (n - 1, n)] {\n        let proof = s.prove_range(st, en).unwrap();\n        // The verifier is given ONLY the requested block bytes.\n        let blocks: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (st..en).map(|i| s.read_block(i).unwrap()).collect();\n        merkle::verify(&proof, bs, data.len() as u64, &root, &blocks).unwrap();\n    }\n\n    // A multi-block interior range also verifies.\n    let proof = s.prove_range(2, 6).unwrap();\n    let blocks: Vec<Vec<u8>> = (2..6).map(|i| s.read_block(i).unwrap()).collect();\n    merkle::verify(&proof, bs, data.len() as u64, &root, &blocks).unwrap();\n\n    // The last block is the short one (31 -> last block length 3).\n    let last = s.read_block(n - 1).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(last.len(), 3);\n}\n\n// 3. Empty file ------------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[test]\nfn empty_file_has_sentinel_root_and_verifies() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"empty\");\n    let s = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, 16).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(s.block_count(), 0);\n    assert_eq!(s.data_len(), 0);\n    assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), empty_root());\n\n    // The canonical empty proof: range [0,0), no nodes, against the sentinel.\n    let proof = RangeProof { n: 0, start: 0, end: 0, nodes: vec![] };\n    merkle::verify(&proof, 16, 0, &empty_root(), &[]).unwrap();\n\n    // Empty proof against a non-empty root must fail.\n    assert_eq!(\n        merkle::verify(&proof, 16, 0, &[1u8; 32], &[]).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::EmptyRootMismatch\n    );\n\n    // Building data then resetting to empty restores the sentinel.\n    let dir2 = tempdir(\"empty2\");\n    let mut s2 = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir2, 16).unwrap();\n    s2.reset(b\"hello\").unwrap();\n    assert_ne!(s2.root().unwrap(), empty_root());\n    s2.reset(b\"\").unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(s2.root().unwrap(), empty_root());\n}\n\n// 4. Forged length ---------------------------------------------------------\n\n#[test]\nfn forged_length_is_rejected() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"forgelen\");\n    let bs = 4u64;\n    let data = b\"abcde\";\n    let mut s = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, bs).unwrap();\n    s.reset(data).unwrap();\n    let root = s.root().unwrap();\n\n    // Honest last-block proof (block 2, one byte).\n    let proof = s.prove_range(2, 3).unwrap();\n    let good = vec![b\"e\".to_vec()];\n    merkle::verify(&proof, bs, 5, &root, &good).unwrap();\n\n    // 4a. Padding the short last block to full size is caught at the leaf.\n    assert!(matches!(\n        merkle::verify(&proof, bs, 8, &root, &[b\"e\\0\\0\\0\".to_vec()]).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::LengthMismatch | ProofError::LeafMismatch { .. }\n    ));\n\n    // 4c. Wrong trusted root with an otherwise valid proof.\n    assert_eq!(\n        merkle::verify(&proof, bs, 5, &[0u8; 32], &good).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::RootMismatch\n    );\n}\n\n// 5. Displaced / misaligned proofs ----------------------------------------\n\n#[test]\nfn misaligned_proofs_are_rejected() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"misalign\");\n    let bs = 4u64;\n    let data = b\"abcdefghijkl\"; // 12 bytes, 3 blocks\n    let mut s = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, bs).unwrap();\n    s.reset(data).unwrap();\n    let root = s.root().unwrap();\n    let good = s.prove_range(1, 2).unwrap();\n    let blocks = vec![b\"efgh\".to_vec()];\n    merkle::verify(&good, bs, 12, &root, &blocks).unwrap();\n\n    // 5a. Retag a node to the wrong index.\n    let mut p = good.clone();\n    p.nodes[1].index = 5;\n    assert!(matches!(\n        merkle::verify(&p, bs, 12, &root, &blocks).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::MisalignedNode { .. }\n    ));\n\n    // 5c. Truncated / extended proofs.\n    let mut p = good.clone();\n    p.nodes.pop();\n    assert_eq!(\n        merkle::verify(&p, bs, 12, &root, &blocks).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::ProofTooShort\n    );\n    let mut p = good.clone();\n    p.nodes.push(ProofNode { level: 3, index: 3, hash: [9u8; 32] });\n    assert_eq!(\n        merkle::verify(&p, bs, 12, &root, &blocks).unwrap_err(),\n        ProofError::ProofTooLong\n    );\n\n    // 5d. Present a proof generated for a different file length.\n    let mut s2 = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &tempdir(\"misalign2\"), bs).unwrap();\n    s2.reset(b\"abcdefghijklm\").unwrap(); // 13 bytes, still 4? no -> 4 blocks\n    let foreign = s2.prove_range(1, 2).unwrap();\n    // The foreign proof's tree shape may still structurally verify up to a\n    // different root; it must at minimum fail the root binding.\n    let err = merkle::verify(&foreign, bs, 12, &root, &blocks).unwrap_err();\n    assert!(\n        matches!(\n            err,\n            ProofError::RootMismatch\n                | ProofError::LengthMismatch\n                | ProofError::MisalignedNode { .. }\n                | ProofError::ProofTooShort\n                | ProofError::LeafMismatch { .. }\n        ),\n        \"unexpected acceptance of foreign proof: {err:?}\"\n    );\n}\n\n// 6. Incremental update cost ----------------------------------------------\n\n#[test]\nfn incremental_update_writes_only_one_path() {\n    use merkle_store::vfs::Vfs;\n    let inner = merkle_store::vfs::MemVfs::new();\n    let bs = 1u64;\n    // Build a 256-leaf tree via a full reset.\n    {\n        let mut s = Store::create(inner.clone(), Path::new(\"/cost\"), bs).unwrap();\n        let data: Vec<u8> = (0..256u16).map(|i| i as u8).collect();\n        s.reset(&data).unwrap();\n    }\n    // Overwrite a single leaf on an instrumented VFS.\n    let vfs = FaultyVfs::new(inner.clone());\n    let mut s = Store::open(vfs.clone(), Path::new(\"/cost\")).unwrap();\n    s.put_block(100, &[0xAB]).unwrap();\n\n    // Exactly one 32-byte write per tree level on the affected path; the\n    // tree has 256 leaves -> 9 levels (0..=8).\n    let mut level_writes = 0u64;\n    for lvl in 0..16 {\n        let path = format!(\"level-{lvl}.bin\");\n        let n = vfs.call_count(Op::WriteAt, &path);\n        level_writes += n;\n        if lvl <= 8 {\n            assert_eq!(n, 1, \"expected exactly one write to {path}\");\n        } else {\n            assert_eq!(n, 0, \"no level {lvl} file should exist\");\n        }\n    }\n    assert_eq!(level_writes, 9, \"one node per level on the path\");\n    // data.bin gets exactly one pwrite as well.\n    assert_eq!(vfs.call_count(Op::WriteAt, \"data.bin\"), 1);\n}\n\n// 7. Crash recovery through every journaled step on a real filesystem ------\n\n#[test]\nfn real_fs_crash_replay_at_every_step() {\n    // Two-block append; instrumented writes fail at call N. After reopen the\n    // repository is internally consistent (root matches a full rebuild).\n    for rule in 1u64..=5 {\n        let dir = tempdir(&format!(\"crash-{rule}\"));\n        {\n            let mut base = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, 4).unwrap();\n            base.put_block(0, b\"abcd\").unwrap();\n        }\n        {\n            let vfs = FaultyVfs::new(RealVfs::new())\n                .fail_on(Op::WriteAtomic, None, rule)\n                .fail_on(Op::WriteAt, None, rule);\n            let mut s = Store::open(vfs, &dir).unwrap();\n            let _ = s.put_block(1, b\"efgh\");\n        }\n        let mut s = open_real(&dir);\n        let data = s.read_data().unwrap();\n        let root = s.root().unwrap();\n        // Whatever survived, the committed root must equal a full rebuild of\n        // exactly the bytes present in data.bin.\n        assert_eq!(root, full_rebuild_root(&data, 4), \"rule {rule}\");\n        assert!(data == b\"abcd\" || data == b\"abcdefgh\", \"rule {rule}: {data:?}\");\n        // The store is usable after recovery.\n        s.force_full_rebuild().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), full_rebuild_root(&data, 4));\n    }\n}\n\n// 8. Incremental update cost ----------------------------------------------\n\n#[test]\nfn incremental_update_writes_only_one_path() {\n    use merkle_store::vfs::Vfs;\n    let inner = merkle_store::vfs::MemVfs::new();\n    let bs = 1u64;\n    // Build a 256-leaf tree via a full reset.\n    {\n        let mut s = Store::create(inner.clone(), Path::new(\"/cost\"), bs).unwrap();\n        let data: Vec<u8> = (0..256u16).map(|i| i as u8).collect();\n        s.reset(&data).unwrap();\n    }\n    // Overwrite a single leaf on an instrumented VFS.\n    let vfs = FaultyVfs::new(inner.clone());\n    let mut s = Store::open(vfs.clone(), Path::new(\"/cost\")).unwrap();\n    s.put_block(100, &[0xAB]).unwrap();\n\n    // Exactly one 32-byte write per tree level on the affected path; the\n    // tree has 256 leaves -> 9 levels (0..=8).\n    let mut level_writes = 0u64;\n    for lvl in 0..16 {\n        let path = format!(\"level-{lvl}.bin\");\n        let n = vfs.call_count(Op::WriteAt, &path);\n        level_writes += n;\n        if lvl <= 8 {\n            assert_eq!(n, 1, \"expected exactly one write to {path}\");\n        } else {\n            assert_eq!(n, 0, \"no level {lvl} file should exist\");\n        }\n    }\n    assert_eq!(level_writes, 9, \"one node per level on the path\");\n    // data.bin gets exactly one pwrite as well.\n    assert_eq!(vfs.call_count(Op::WriteAt, \"data.bin\"), 1);\n}\n\n// 7. Crash recovery through every journaled step on a real filesystem ------\n\n#[test]\nfn real_fs_crash_replay_at_every_step() {\n    // Two-block append; instrumented writes fail at call N. After reopen the\n    // repository is internally consistent (root matches a full rebuild).\n    for rule in 1u64..=5 {\n        let dir = tempdir(&format!(\"crash-{rule}\"));\n        {\n            let mut base = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, 4).unwrap();\n            base.put_block(0, b\"abcd\").unwrap();\n        }\n        {\n            let vfs = FaultyVfs::new(RealVfs::new())\n                .fail_on(Op::WriteAtomic, None, rule)\n                .fail_on(Op::WriteAt, None, rule);\n            let mut s = Store::open(vfs, &dir).unwrap();\n            let _ = s.put_block(1, b\"efgh\");\n        }\n        let mut s = open_real(&dir);\n        let data = s.read_data().unwrap();\n        let root = s.root().unwrap();\n        // Whatever survived, the committed root must equal a full rebuild of\n        // exactly the bytes present in data.bin.\n        assert_eq!(root, full_rebuild_root(&data, 4), \"rule {rule}\");\n        assert!(data == b\"abcd\" || data == b\"abcdefgh\", \"rule {rule}: {data:?}\");\n        // The store is usable after recovery.\n        s.force_full_rebuild().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(s.root().unwrap(), full_rebuild_root(&data, 4));\n    }\n}\n\n// 8. Cross-check verifier against the store over many shapes --------------\n\n#[test]\nfn exhaustive_range_verification_small_trees() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"exhaustive\");\n    for bs in 1u64..=5 {\n        for nblocks in 0usize..10 {\n            let mut d = tempdir(&format!(\"ex-{bs}-{nblocks}\"));\n            let payload: Vec<u8> = (0..(nblocks as u64 * bs)).map(|i| (i % 199) as u8).collect();\n            let mut s = Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &d, bs).unwrap();\n            s.reset(&payload).unwrap();\n            let root = s.root().unwrap();\n            if nblocks == 0 {\n                let p = s.prove_range(0, 0).unwrap();\n                merkle::verify(&p, bs, 0, &root, &[]).unwrap();\n                continue;\n            }\n            for st in 0..nblocks {\n                for en in st + 1..=nblocks {\n                    let p = s.prove_range(st as u64, en as u64).unwrap();\n                    let blocks: Vec<Vec<u8>> =\n                        (st..en).map(|i| s.read_block(i as u64).unwrap()).collect();\n                    merkle::verify(&p, bs, payload.len() as u64, &root, &blocks)\n                        .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!(\"bs={bs} n={nblocks} {st}..{en}: {e}\"));\n                }\n            }\n            // silence unused mut on platforms\n            let _ = &mut d;\n        }\n    }\n}\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"05462e2e-2089-4ff5-8db1-f0364cfb568d","session_id":"7f404cf2-9b88-493e-b8e2-bb5bcd9a4e01","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp10/a","sessionId":"7f404cf2-9b88-493e-b8e2-bb5bcd9a4e01","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"ab/run-20260922T151547Z/opp10-a","slug":"steady-napping-thunder"}

End-to-end HTTP tests against a real loopback TCP server.\n//!\n//! Demonstrates the verifier boundary: a SECOND server instance (or any\n//! process) verifies a /range response using only the JSON in that response\n//! plus a trusted root — it never opens the repository under test.\n\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::TcpStream;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::thread;\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nuse merkle_store::api::RepoHandler;\nuse merkle_store::http;\nuse merkle_store::json::{self, Json};\nuse merkle_store::store::Store;\nuse merkle_store::vfs::{MemVfs, RealVfs};\n\nfn tempdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    let mut d = std::env::temp_dir();\n    d.push(format!(\n        \"merkle-store-http-{}-{}-{}\",\n        tag,\n        std::process::id(),\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .unwrap()\n            .as_nanos()\n    ));\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&d).unwrap();\n    d\n}\n\nstruct RawResponse {\n    status: u16,\n    body: String,\n}\n\nfn request(addr: &str, method: &str, target: &str, body: &[u8]) -> RawResponse {\n    let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).unwrap();\n    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5))).unwrap();\n    let head = format!(\n        \"{method} {target} HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: {addr}\\r\\nContent-Type: application/octet-stream\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n\",\n        body.len()\n    );\n    stream.write_all(head.as_bytes()).unwrap();\n    stream.write_all(body).unwrap();\n    let mut raw = Vec::new();\n    stream.read_to_end(&mut raw).unwrap();\n    let split = raw.windows(4).position(|w| w == b\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\").unwrap() + 4;\n    let status = String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw[..20]);\n    let status = status.split_whitespace().nth(1).unwrap().parse().unwrap();\n    RawResponse {\n        status,\n        body: String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw[split..]).into_owned(),\n    }\n}\n\nfn spawn_server(handler: Arc<RepoHandler>) -> String {\n    let listener = std::net::TcpListener::bind(\"127.0.0.1:0\").unwrap();\n    let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap().to_string();\n    thread::spawn(move || {\n        let _ = http::serve(listener, handler);\n    });\n    // Wait briefly for the thread to accept.\n    thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));\n    addr\n}\n\nfn spawn_real_store(dir: &std::path::Path) -> String {\n    let store = Store::open(RealVfs::new(), dir).unwrap();\n    spawn_server(RepoHandler::shared(store))\n}\n\n/// A verifier server backed by an EMPTY in-memory FS — proving it never\n/// touches the target repository's files during /verify.\nfn spawn_stateless_verifier() -> String {\n    // RepoHandler wraps a Store; give it an unrelated empty MemVfs repo.\n    let mut store = Store::create(MemVfs::new(), std::path::Path::new(\"/verifier\"), 4).unwrap();\n    store.reset(b\"\").unwrap();\n    spawn_server(RepoHandler::shared(store))\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn http_build_root_range_and_verify() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"flow\");\n    {\n        Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, 4).unwrap();\n    }\n    let addr = spawn_real_store(&dir);\n    let verifier = spawn_stateless_verifier();\n\n    // health\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/health\", b\"\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n    assert!(r.body.contains(\"\\\"status\\\": \\\"ok\\\"\"));\n\n    // build full file\n    let payload = b\"abcdefghijk\"; // 11 bytes -> 3 blocks (4,4,3)\n    let r = request(&addr, \"POST\", \"/build\", payload);\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n    let build = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(build.get(\"n\").and_then(Json::as_i64), Some(3));\n    let trusted_root = build.get(\"root\").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().to_string();\n\n    // root endpoint agrees\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/root\", b\"\");\n    let rootj = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(rootj.get(\"root\").unwrap().as_str(), Some(trusted_root.as_str()));\n\n    // first range\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/range?which=first\", b\"\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n    let range1 = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(range1.get(\"start\").and_then(Json::as_i64), Some(0));\n    // The response already carries everything the verifier needs.\n    assert!(range1.get(\"proof\").unwrap().as_array().unwrap().len() >= 1);\n\n    // Verify on the independent verifier server: reuse the response JSON,\n    // injecting the trusted root.\n    let mut verify_body = range1.clone();\n    if let json::Json::Object(ref mut m) = verify_body {\n        m.insert(\"root\".to_string(), Json::Str(trusted_root.clone()));\n    }\n    let text = verify_body.compact();\n    let r = request(&verifier, \"POST\", \"/verify\", text.as_bytes());\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n    let v = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"valid\").and_then(Json::as_bool), Some(true), \"body: {}\", r.body);\n\n    // last range (short block) verifies too\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/range?which=last\", b\"\");\n    let range_last = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    let mut body = range_last.clone();\n    if let json::Json::Object(ref mut m) = body {\n        m.insert(\"root\".to_string(), Json::Str(trusted_root.clone()));\n    }\n    let r = request(&verifier, \"POST\", \"/verify\", body.compact().as_bytes());\n    let v = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"valid\").and_then(Json::as_bool), Some(true));\n\n    // tamper one block byte -> invalid\n    let mut tampered = range1.clone();\n    if let json::Json::Object(ref mut m) = tampered {\n        m.insert(\"root\".to_string(), Json::Str(trusted_root.clone()));\n        if let Some(Json::Array(blocks)) = m.get_mut(\"blocks\") {\n            if let Json::Object(first) = &mut blocks[0] {\n                let enc = first.get(\"data\").unwrap().as_str().unwrap();\n                let mut bytes = merkle_store::base64::decode(enc).unwrap();\n                bytes[0] ^= 0x01;\n                first.insert(\"data\".to_string(), Json::Str(merkle_store::base64::encode(&bytes)));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    let r = request(&verifier, \"POST\", \"/verify\", tampered.compact().as_bytes());\n    let v = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"valid\").and_then(Json::as_bool), Some(false));\n    assert!(v.get(\"error\").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().contains(\"mismatch\"));\n\n    // forged length -> invalid\n    let mut forged = range1.clone();\n    if let json::Json::Object(ref mut m) = forged {\n        m.insert(\"root\".to_string(), Json::Str(trusted_root.clone()));\n        m.insert(\"data_len\".to_string(), Json::Int(99));\n    }\n    let r = request(&verifier, \"POST\", \"/verify\", forged.compact().as_bytes());\n    let v = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"valid\").and_then(Json::as_bool), Some(false));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn http_empty_file_verifies() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"emptyhttp\");\n    Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, 8).unwrap();\n    let addr = spawn_real_store(&dir);\n    let verifier = spawn_stateless_verifier();\n\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/range?which=first\", b\"\");\n    let range = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    let mut body = range;\n    if let json::Json::Object(ref mut m) = body {\n        // Pull the committed empty-root sentinel from /root.\n        let rj = json::parse(&request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/root\", b\"\").body).unwrap();\n        m.insert(\n            \"root\".to_string(),\n            Json::Str(rj.get(\"root\").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().to_string()),\n        );\n    }\n    let r = request(&verifier, \"POST\", \"/verify\", body.compact().as_bytes());\n    let v = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"valid\").and_then(Json::as_bool), Some(true), \"{}\", r.body);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn http_put_block_incremental_and_errors() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"puthttp\");\n    Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, 4).unwrap();\n    let addr = spawn_real_store(&dir);\n\n    let r = request(&addr, \"PUT\", \"/block?index=0\", b\"abcd\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n    let r = request(&addr, \"PUT\", \"/block?index=1\", b\"ef\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n\n    // Appending while the last block is short is rejected (400).\n    let r = request(&addr, \"PUT\", \"/block?index=2\", b\"ghij\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 400);\n\n    // Fill the last block to full, then appending works.\n    let r = request(&addr, \"PUT\", \"/block?index=1\", b\"efgh\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n    let r = request(&addr, \"PUT\", \"/block?index=2\", b\"ij\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/root\", b\"\");\n    let v = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"data_len\").and_then(Json::as_i64), Some(10));\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"n\").and_then(Json::as_i64), Some(3));\n\n    // Unknown route.\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/nope\", b\"\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 404);\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_a2720fc7decd5a9f77d3d79f","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":5145,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":135992,"output_tokens":2827,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_qmucan093f40wo1goc41wjlq":{"content":"//! End-to-end HTTP tests against a real loopback TCP server.\n//!\n//! Demonstrates the verifier boundary: a SECOND server instance (or any\n//! process) verifies a /range response using only the JSON in that response\n//! plus a trusted root — it never opens the repository under test.\n\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::TcpStream;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::thread;\nuse std::time::Duration;\n\nuse merkle_store::api::RepoHandler;\nuse merkle_store::http;\nuse merkle_store::json::{self, Json};\nuse merkle_store::store::Store;\nuse merkle_store::vfs::{MemVfs, RealVfs};\n\nfn tempdir(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    let mut d = std::env::temp_dir();\n    d.push(format!(\n        \"merkle-store-http-{}-{}-{}\",\n        tag,\n        std::process::id(),\n        std::time::SystemTime::now()\n            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)\n            .unwrap()\n            .as_nanos()\n    ));\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&d).unwrap();\n    d\n}\n\nstruct RawResponse {\n    status: u16,\n    body: String,\n}\n\nfn request(addr: &str, method: &str, target: &str, body: &[u8]) -> RawResponse {\n    let mut stream = TcpStream::connect(addr).unwrap();\n    stream.set_read_timeout(Some(Duration::from_secs(5))).unwrap();\n    let head = format!(\n        \"{method} {target} HTTP/1.1\\r\\nHost: {addr}\\r\\nContent-Type: application/octet-stream\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n\",\n        body.len()\n    );\n    stream.write_all(head.as_bytes()).unwrap();\n    stream.write_all(body).unwrap();\n    let mut raw = Vec::new();\n    stream.read_to_end(&mut raw).unwrap();\n    let split = raw.windows(4).position(|w| w == b\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\").unwrap() + 4;\n    let status = String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw[..20]);\n    let status = status.split_whitespace().nth(1).unwrap().parse().unwrap();\n    RawResponse {\n        status,\n        body: String::from_utf8_lossy(&raw[split..]).into_owned(),\n    }\n}\n\nfn spawn_server(handler: Arc<RepoHandler>) -> String {\n    let listener = std::net::TcpListener::bind(\"127.0.0.1:0\").unwrap();\n    let addr = listener.local_addr().unwrap().to_string();\n    thread::spawn(move || {\n        let _ = http::serve(listener, handler);\n    });\n    // Wait briefly for the thread to accept.\n    thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50));\n    addr\n}\n\nfn spawn_real_store(dir: &std::path::Path) -> String {\n    let store = Store::open(RealVfs::new(), dir).unwrap();\n    spawn_server(RepoHandler::shared(store))\n}\n\n/// A verifier server backed by an EMPTY in-memory FS — proving it never\n/// touches the target repository's files during /verify.\nfn spawn_stateless_verifier() -> String {\n    // RepoHandler wraps a Store; give it an unrelated empty MemVfs repo.\n    let mut store = Store::create(MemVfs::new(), std::path::Path::new(\"/verifier\"), 4).unwrap();\n    store.reset(b\"\").unwrap();\n    spawn_server(RepoHandler::shared(store))\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn http_build_root_range_and_verify() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"flow\");\n    {\n        Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, 4).unwrap();\n    }\n    let addr = spawn_real_store(&dir);\n    let verifier = spawn_stateless_verifier();\n\n    // health\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/health\", b\"\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n    assert!(r.body.contains(\"\\\"status\\\": \\\"ok\\\"\"));\n\n    // build full file\n    let payload = b\"abcdefghijk\"; // 11 bytes -> 3 blocks (4,4,3)\n    let r = request(&addr, \"POST\", \"/build\", payload);\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n    let build = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(build.get(\"n\").and_then(Json::as_i64), Some(3));\n    let trusted_root = build.get(\"root\").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().to_string();\n\n    // root endpoint agrees\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/root\", b\"\");\n    let rootj = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(rootj.get(\"root\").unwrap().as_str(), Some(trusted_root.as_str()));\n\n    // first range\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/range?which=first\", b\"\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n    let range1 = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(range1.get(\"start\").and_then(Json::as_i64), Some(0));\n    // The response already carries everything the verifier needs.\n    assert!(range1.get(\"proof\").unwrap().as_array().unwrap().len() >= 1);\n\n    // Verify on the independent verifier server: reuse the response JSON,\n    // injecting the trusted root.\n    let mut verify_body = range1.clone();\n    if let json::Json::Object(ref mut m) = verify_body {\n        m.insert(\"root\".to_string(), Json::Str(trusted_root.clone()));\n    }\n    let text = verify_body.compact();\n    let r = request(&verifier, \"POST\", \"/verify\", text.as_bytes());\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n    let v = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"valid\").and_then(Json::as_bool), Some(true), \"body: {}\", r.body);\n\n    // last range (short block) verifies too\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/range?which=last\", b\"\");\n    let range_last = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    let mut body = range_last.clone();\n    if let json::Json::Object(ref mut m) = body {\n        m.insert(\"root\".to_string(), Json::Str(trusted_root.clone()));\n    }\n    let r = request(&verifier, \"POST\", \"/verify\", body.compact().as_bytes());\n    let v = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"valid\").and_then(Json::as_bool), Some(true));\n\n    // tamper one block byte -> invalid\n    let mut tampered = range1.clone();\n    if let json::Json::Object(ref mut m) = tampered {\n        m.insert(\"root\".to_string(), Json::Str(trusted_root.clone()));\n        if let Some(Json::Array(blocks)) = m.get_mut(\"blocks\") {\n            if let Json::Object(first) = &mut blocks[0] {\n                let enc = first.get(\"data\").unwrap().as_str().unwrap();\n                let mut bytes = merkle_store::base64::decode(enc).unwrap();\n                bytes[0] ^= 0x01;\n                first.insert(\"data\".to_string(), Json::Str(merkle_store::base64::encode(&bytes)));\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    let r = request(&verifier, \"POST\", \"/verify\", tampered.compact().as_bytes());\n    let v = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"valid\").and_then(Json::as_bool), Some(false));\n    assert!(v.get(\"error\").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().contains(\"mismatch\"));\n\n    // forged length -> invalid\n    let mut forged = range1.clone();\n    if let json::Json::Object(ref mut m) = forged {\n        m.insert(\"root\".to_string(), Json::Str(trusted_root.clone()));\n        m.insert(\"data_len\".to_string(), Json::Int(99));\n    }\n    let r = request(&verifier, \"POST\", \"/verify\", forged.compact().as_bytes());\n    let v = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"valid\").and_then(Json::as_bool), Some(false));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn http_empty_file_verifies() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"emptyhttp\");\n    Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, 8).unwrap();\n    let addr = spawn_real_store(&dir);\n    let verifier = spawn_stateless_verifier();\n\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/range?which=first\", b\"\");\n    let range = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    let mut body = range;\n    if let json::Json::Object(ref mut m) = body {\n        // Pull the committed empty-root sentinel from /root.\n        let rj = json::parse(&request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/root\", b\"\").body).unwrap();\n        m.insert(\n            \"root\".to_string(),\n            Json::Str(rj.get(\"root\").unwrap().as_str().unwrap().to_string()),\n        );\n    }\n    let r = request(&verifier, \"POST\", \"/verify\", body.compact().as_bytes());\n    let v = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"valid\").and_then(Json::as_bool), Some(true), \"{}\", r.body);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn http_put_block_incremental_and_errors() {\n    let dir = tempdir(\"puthttp\");\n    Store::create(RealVfs::new(), &dir, 4).unwrap();\n    let addr = spawn_real_store(&dir);\n\n    let r = request(&addr, \"PUT\", \"/block?index=0\", b\"abcd\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n    let r = request(&addr, \"PUT\", \"/block?index=1\", b\"ef\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n\n    // Appending while the last block is short is rejected (400).\n    let r = request(&addr, \"PUT\", \"/block?index=2\", b\"ghij\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 400);\n\n    // Fill the last block to full, then appending works.\n    let r = request(&addr, \"PUT\", \"/block?index=1\", b\"efgh\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n    let r = request(&addr, \"PUT\", \"/block?index=2\", b\"ij\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, 200);\n\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/root\", b\"\");\n    let v = json::parse(&r.body).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"data_len\").and_then(Json::as_i64), Some(10));\n    assert_eq!(v.get(\"n\").and_then(Json::as_i64), Some(3));\n\n    // Unknown route.\n    let r = request(&addr, \"GET\", \"/nope\", b\"\");\n    assert_eq!(r.status, }\n63\t    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out).into_owned()\n64\t}\n65\t\n66\t#[derive(Debug)]\n67\tpub enum HttpError {\n68\t    BadRequest(&'static str),\n69\t    EntityTooLarge,\n70\t}\n71\t\n72\tfn stream.write_all(&resp.body)?;\n198\t    stream.flush()\n199\t}\n200\t\n201\tpub trait Handler: Send + Sync {\n202\t    fn handle(&self, req: &Request) -> Response;\n203\t}\n204\t\n205\tpub fn match stream {\n209\t            Ok(mut stream) => {\n210\t                let h = Arc::clone(&handler);\n211\t                std::thread::spawn(move || {\n212\t                    let resp = match read_request(&mut stream) {\n213\t                        Ok(req) => h.handle(&req),\n214\t                        Err(HttpError::EntityTooLarge) => Response::error_json(413, \"body too large\"),\n215\t                        Err(HttpError::BadRequest(msg)) => {\n216\t                            Response::error_json(400, msg)\n217\t                        }\n218\t                    };\n219\t                    let _ = write_response(&mut stream, &resp);\n220\t                });\n221\t            }\n222\t            Err(_) => continue,\n223\t        }\n224\t    }\n225\t {"parentUuid":"2d6cbec2-325f-458b-b0b6-944149be800d","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_es9e7o2h5cev67syw4dazii0","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp10/a/scripts/demo.sh","content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Reproducible end-to-end demo for merkle-store.\n# Builds a repo, serves it over HTTP, fetches range proofs, and verifies\n# them both online (independent verifier process) and offline (CLI).\n#\n# Usage:  bash scripts/demo.sh\nset -euo pipefail\n\nROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/..\" && pwd)\"\nBIN=\"$ROOT/target/release/merkle-store\"\nWORK=\"$(mktemp -d -t merkle-demo-XXXXXX)\"\nADDR=\"127.0.0.1:18280\"\nVADDR=\"127.0.0.1:18281\"\n\nif [[ ! -x \"$BIN\" ]]; then\n  echo \"building release binary…\"\n  cargo build --release --manifest-path \"$ROOT/Cargo.toml\" >/dev/null\nfi\n\nsay() { printf '\\n\\033[1;36m== %s ==\\033[0m\\n' \"$*\"; }\ncleanup() {\n  [[ -n \"${SRV_PID:-}\" ]] && kill \"$SRV_PID\" 2>/dev/null || true\n  [[ -n \"${VRF_PID:-}\" ]] && kill \"$VRF_PID\" 2>/dev/null || true\n}\ntrap cleanup EXIT\n\nsay \"work dir: $WORK\"\nREPO=\"$WORK/repo\"; VRF=\"$WORK/verifier\"\n\"$BIN\" init \"$REPO\" --block-size 4\n\nsay \"start server on $ADDR\"\n\"$BIN\" serve \"$REPO\" --addr \"$ADDR\" &\nSRV_PID=$!\nsleep 0.3\n\nsay \"build an 11-byte file (3 blocks of 4/4/3)\"\nprintf 'abcdefghijk' > \"$WORK/payload.bin\"\ncurl -s -X POST --data-binary \"@$WORK/payload.bin\" \"http://$ADDR/build\"\necho\n\nROOT_B64=$(curl -s \"$ADDR/root\" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)[\"root\"])')\nsay \"trusted root: $ROOT_B64\"\n\nsay \"first-block range proof\"\ncurl -s \"$ADDR/range?which=first\" | tee \"$WORK/first.json\"\necho\n\nsay \"last-block (short) range proof\"\ncurl -s \"$ADDR/range?which=last\" | tee \"$WORK/last.json\"\necho\n\n# A second, completely independent verifier rooted at an EMPTY repo.\n\"$BIN\" init \"$VRF\" --block-size 4\n\"$BIN\" serve \"$VRF\" --addr \"$VADDR\" &\nVRF_PID=$!\nsleep 0.3\n\nsay \"verify first proof on the INDEPENDENT verifier ($VADDR, empty repo)\"\ncurl -s -X POST --data-binary \"@$WORK/first.json\" \"http://$VADDR/verify\"; echo\nsay \"verify last proof on the INDEPENDENT verifier\"\ncurl -s -X POST --data-binary \"@$WORK/last.json\" \"http://$VADDR/verify\"; echo\n\nsay \"offline CLI verify (no server)\"\n\"$BIN\" verify \"$WORK/first.json\"; echo\n\nsay \"negative tests: tampered block byte\"\npython3 - \"$WORK/first.json\" \"$WORK/bad-block.json\" <<'PY'\nimport sys,json,base64\nd=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))\nb=bytearray(base64.b64decode(d[\"blocks\"][0][\"data\"])); b[0]^=1\nd[\"blocks\"][0][\"data\"]=base64.b64encode(b).decode()\njson.dump(d,open(sys.argv[2],\"w\"))\nPY\n\"$BIN\" verify \"$WORK/bad-block.json\"; echo \"exit=$?\"\n\nsay \"negative tests: forged data_len\"\nsed 's/\"data_len\": 11/\"data_len\": 99/' \"$WORK/first.json\" > \"$WORK/bad-len.json\"\n\"$BIN\" verify \"$WORK/bad-len.json\"; echo \"exit=$?\"\n\nsay \"negative tests: swapped (misaligned) proof nodes\"\npython3 - \"$WORK/first.json\" \"$WORK/bad-proof.json\" <<'PY'\nimport sys,json\nd=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))\nd[\"proof\"][1],d[\"proof\"][2]=d[\"proof\"][2],d[\"proof\"][1]\njson.dump(d,open(sys.argv[2],\"w\"))\nPY\n\"$BIN\" verify \"$WORK/bad-proof.json\"; echo \"exit=$?\"\n\nsay \"empty file: reset to empty and verify\"\ncurl -s -X POST --data '' \"$ADDR/build\" >/dev/null\ncurl -s \"$ADDR/range?which=first\" > \"$WORK/empty.json\"\ncat \"$WORK/empty.json\"; echo\ncurl -s -X POST --data-binary \"@$WORK/empty.json\" \"http://$VADDR/verify\"; echo\n\nsay \"demo complete; working copy kept at: $WORK\"\ntrap - EXIT\ncleanup\necho \"repo left in $WORK\"\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_c260c20822658320d7ea7c07","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":1023,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":168760,"output_tokens":1498,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_es9e7o2h5cev67syw4dazii0":{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Reproducible end-to-end demo for merkle-store.\n# Builds a repo, serves it over HTTP, fetches range proofs, and verifies\n# them both online (independent verifier process) and offline (CLI).\n#\n# Usage:  bash scripts/demo.sh\nset -euo pipefail\n\nROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")/..\" && pwd)\"\nBIN=\"$ROOT/target/release/merkle-store\"\nWORK=\"$(mktemp -d -t merkle-demo-XXXXXX)\"\nADDR=\"127.0.0.1:18280\"\nVADDR=\"127.0.0.1:18281\"\n\nif [[ ! -x \"$BIN\" ]];
